#### 19.3 The tests as a contract

##### 19.3.1 Inventory, and the numbers as measured

Five test modules plus one shared fixture module cover this package. All live in
`Tensile/Tests/unit/`. Counts below are **collected test counts**, not `def test_` counts — the
difference is large because several suites are parametrized over a loop-order × split × prefetch
matrix.

| file | lines | collected | primary targets |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `Tests/unit/test_gir.py` | 4835 | **602** | everything under `gir/`, plus `loopir_to_gir.py`, plus the address arithmetic in `lds_geometry.py` |
| `Tests/unit/test_gir_to_rocisa.py` | 359 | **29** | `gir/emit_plan.py` (the pure half of layer 3) and the non-emitting parts of `gir_to_rocisa.py` |
| `Tests/unit/test_value_placement.py` | 204 | **11** | `gir/analyses/value_placement.py`, and **nothing else** |
| `Tests/unit/test_uniform_placement.py` | 197 | **13** | `gir/analyses/uniform_placement.py` and `uniform_emission.py` |
| `Tests/unit/test_tdm_split.py` | 410 | **47** | `tdm_split.py`, `lds_geometry.py`, `region_derivation_check.py` |
| `Tests/unit/gir_fixtures.py` | 39 | — | the six shared parameter dictionaries and `theta(params)` |
| | | **702** | |

A further ~12 tests in `Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py` cross the boundary into this package: they
call `build_gir`, `render_gir`, `plan_block` and `plan_quantum` to check that a θ decision survives
the lowering, and one asserts that the two independent definitions of the hazard-kind vocabulary
(one in layer 1's dependency ledger, one in `gir/analyses/lds_hazards.py`) do not collide.

##### 19.3.2 Running the suite without the compiled instruction extension

This matters more than it sounds, because it is the single design constraint that shapes the whole
`gir/` package: **`gir/` imports nothing from the compiled instruction-generation extension**, so
the entire graph, analysis, pass, verifier and emit-plan stack is exercisable under a plain
CPython with no ROCm toolchain, no GPU and no C++ build. The one upward import in the whole
subpackage is `gir/analyses/dep_defuse.py:19`, which reaches into layer 1 for a pure-Python
predicate.

The obstacle is not the tests — it is `Tests/unit/conftest.py:5`, which does
`from streamk5_test_helpers import mock_streamk_writer`, and that module's line 10 does
`from Tensile.KernelWriterAssembly import KernelWriterAssembly`, which imports the extension at
module scope. So the naive invocation fails during **conftest collection**, before a single test
runs:

```
$ python3 -m pytest Tensile/Tests/unit/test_gir.py
ImportError while loading conftest '.../Tensile/Tests/unit/conftest.py'.
  Tensile/Tests/unit/streamk5_test_helpers.py:10: in <module>
      from Tensile.KernelWriterAssembly import KernelWriterAssembly
  E   ImportError: cannot import name 'rocIsa' from 'rocisa'
```

The working invocation is `--noconftest` plus an explicit `PYTHONPATH`, run from the test
directory (the conftest is also what normally puts the package root on `sys.path`):

```
$ cd Tensile/Tests/unit
$ PYTHONPATH=<tensilelite-root> python3 -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider \
      test_gir.py test_gir_to_rocisa.py test_value_placement.py \
      test_uniform_placement.py test_tdm_split.py
```

Measured on a tree with the extension unbuilt: **683 passed, 19 failed**, and every one of the 19
failures is an extension import, not a logic failure. Per file:

| file | without the extension |
|---|---|
| `test_gir.py` | **602 / 602 pass** |
| `test_value_placement.py` | **11 / 11 pass** |
| `test_tdm_split.py` | **47 / 47 pass** |
| `test_uniform_placement.py` | 8 pass, 5 fail (`ModuleNotFoundError: rocisa.code` — the emission-layer half builds real instruction `Module`/`Label` nodes) |
| `test_gir_to_rocisa.py` | 15 pass, 14 fail (the register-depth, ring-depth, tag, wrap-lead, prefetch-index, retired-Mark and barrier-strip tests all need real nodes) |

Three consequences for a maintainer:

1. **Any change under `gir/` can be validated in seconds with no build.** `test_gir.py` alone is 602
   assertions and runs in under a minute. There is no excuse for shipping a `gir/` change unrun.
2. **The 14+5 extension-dependent tests are the boundary.** If you are editing `leaves.py`,
   `gir_to_rocisa.py`'s emitting methods, or `uniform_emission.py`'s scanner, you need the built
   extension (`invoke rocisa`) and the normal `tox -e unit` path.
3. **`--noconftest` also drops the `--mn`/`--mt`/`--dump-asm` CLI options** declared in
   `Tests/unit/conftest.py`'s `pytest_addoption` (`:16` — `--mn` at `:18`, `--mt` at `:22`, `--dump-asm` at `:30`) and the autouse `skip_parametrized_if_cli` fixture (`:8`). Neither is
   used by any test in this package, so dropping them is free here — but do not generalize the
   recipe to the whole `Tests/unit` tree.

##### 19.3.3 The shared fixtures: what each one exists to catch

`Tests/unit/gir_fixtures.py` holds six parameter dictionaries and one function,
`theta(params)` (`gir_fixtures.py:38`), which is a one-line wrapper over the θ translator. The
dictionaries are the whole reason the suite generalizes, and each was added **after** a confident
wrong answer that the then-current matrix could not catch. Read them as a list of shapes that have
each broken something:

| fixture | line | the shape it isolates |
|---|---:|---|
| `BF16_NT_KMN` | `:12` | The canonical kernel: a 16×16×32 matrix instruction, `DepthU` 64, wavefront 32, two-deep global prefetch, one-deep local prefetch, a 2×2 wave tile, a 2-deep LDS ring. Everything else is a one-key delta from this. |
| `BF16_NT_KMN_PLR0` | `:26` | Local prefetch off — no read-ahead. The read swap moves from mid-body to the loop bottom, which is a different placement answer from the same analysis. |
| `BF16_NT_KMN_FUSED_XAGENT` | `:29` | The Φ fuse **and** two agents. Both facts at once, which is the shipping multi-wave configuration. |
| `BF16_NT_KMN_FUSED_SAME_AGENT` | `:31` | The same fuse with **one** agent. This exists so a test can tell which of the two facts it is measuring. Before it existed, "cross-agent" and "fused" were confounded in every multi-wave assertion. |
| `BF16_NT_KMN_UNFUSED_MULTIAGENT` | `:34` | Four agents, **no** fuse — a lone operand loaded cooperatively. This is the case that motivated rewriting the cross-agent predicate: the old member-disagreement test returned `False` here, i.e. it said "same agent" for a genuinely cooperative load. |
| `BF16_NT_KMN_1LDS` | `:35` | A ring depth of 1. The degenerate case where a generation stops identifying a chunk at all, so every rotation-based conclusion becomes vacuous and every rotation-based *assumption* becomes wrong. |

`test_gir.py:2211-2219` documents the *policy* behind the set: each family is present because a
previous matrix gave a confident wrong answer on it. When adding a fixture, state the property it
isolates in the same style, and prefer a **one-key delta** from `BF16_NT_KMN` so a failure localizes
to the key.

Larger fixtures are built inline in the test files rather than shared, because they carry
type-specific keys: `_split_theta` (`test_gir.py:484`) for storage-split kernels, `_fused_theta`
(`:594`), `_fp8_kernel` (`:3970`) with its `_Bytes` stand-in data type (`:3961`), `_mx_kernel`
(`:4035`) for the microscaling shapes, and `_q_kernel` / `_wide_load` / `_broadcast` /
`_theta_with_quantum` (`:4291`–`:4317`) for the movement-quantum tests.

##### 19.3.4 `test_gir.py` — what each section pins

602 tests in roughly thirty labelled sections. Rather than list them, here is the mapping from
section to module and, for the sections that encode a historical defect, what the defect was. The
test names are deliberately long sentences; grep them, they are the index.

| section (line) | module under test | contract pinned |
|---|---|---|
| lowering (74) | `loopir_to_gir.py`, `gir/verify.py`, `gir/render.gir_counts` | Op-parity with the layer-1 tree — the same number of loads and multiply-accumulates come out. `_loopir_stage_counts` (`:75`, with nested `walk` `:77`, `find_peel` `:112`, `find_steady` `:125`) counts the tree side independently of the lowering. |
| gen_reaching (214) | `gir/analyses/gen_reaching.py` | The concrete generation each access resolves to, including the all-zero answer at ring 1. |
| swap dataflow (241) | `gir/analyses/swap_regions.py`, `gir/region.py` | Where each buffer-pointer flip lands, per hop, per pipeline depth. `_swaps` (`:45`) filters the pending marks; `_subject` (`:57`) normalizes a Mark's hop-dependent key to a tuple, and its docstring is explicit that tests asserting the **key itself** must read `mark.at` directly, because the key is the thing under test. |
| reg_band / reg_gen (342) | `gir/analyses/reg_band.py`, `gir/passes/reg_gen.py` | W is consistent per `(operand, group)` at both prefetch depths. |
| tokens / dep_defuse (364) | `gir/passes/tokens.py`, `gir/analyses/dep_defuse.py` | Every token names exactly one buffer; every dependency edge carried from layer 1 is indexed. |
| gr_increment (407) | `gir/analyses/gr_increment.py` | The address advance follows *the copy that used the descriptor*, and the first copy has none. |
| pipeline + build-once (442) | `gir/passes/pipeline.py`, `build_gir` | The pipeline applies its Marks and the result verifies; a second `build_gir` on the same kernel reuses the cached program. |
| per-region completion (483) | `gir/passes/tokens._region_key` | The shared-versus-per-region completion toggle produces the two different token granularities, and **both** verify and discharge. |
| Φ tokens (548) | `gir/passes/tokens._completion_unit`, `_unit_key` | A fused group is one completion; every awaited unit is actually produced. |
| Φ identity (593) | `gir/refs.copy_unit` | `copy_unit` names every member, and **rejects** members that rotate differently. |
| six-axis reorder (776) | `gir/emit_plan.py`, `check_plan` | Every one of the six-axis loop-order words emits and lowers cleanly. |
| structured predicate (898) | `gir/nodes.Pred`/`Bound`, `loopir_to_gir._gir_pred` | The terminator predicate is a struct, not a string, and `_gir_pred` **rejects** a shape `Bound` cannot hold. |
| short-loop arm (962) | `loopir_to_gir._short_steps` | The arm lowers to real blocks with its guard chain; a shape mismatch is rejected. |
| multi-exit headers (1014) | `gir/nodes.CondChain`, `gir/passes/scaffold_map.py` | Chain arms are ordinary forward edges; a missing arm target is rejected; the chain is well-formed by construction. |
| multi-block body (1099) | `loop_copies`, `gir/analyses/cfg.BackEdgeSet.leaving` | The fall-through chain shares one back edge and the residue timeline spans it. |
| `Return` sink (1176) | `gir/nodes.Return`, `cfg.successors` | A sink has no successors and still survives dominance. |
| tail loop (1220) | `gir/verify._check_cfg` | A tail loop is an accepted *second* loop region; a second non-tail loop is still rejected. |

| section (line) | module under test | contract pinned |
|---|---|---|
| pointer def-use gate (1282) | `swap_regions._hop_access` | **An independent oracle**, not a restatement. `_simulate_pointer` (`test_gir.py:1283`) walks the CFG replaying the swaps as a state machine and checks the pointer never reads the wrong buffer, across every loop order, every pipeline depth, and a multi-block body. `_pointer_hops` (`:1331`) enumerates the hops so the oracle covers both. |
| gr_increment dataflow (1398) | `gr_increment._copy_of`, `_chunk_of` | One chunk advance per copy; the first has none. |
| placement policy (1490) | `gir/passes/placement.py`, `EARLIEST`/`MIDPOINT` | Descriptor changes land at the **earliest** point of their window; the LDS read swap lands **mid**-window and specifically *not* at its earliest point. `_is_read` (`:1491`) and `_is_copy_of` (`:1496`) classify the body nodes. |
| bridge: the fuse is derived (1593) | layer-1 bridge ↔ `refs.copy_unit` | The fuse flag reaches θ as a **group**, and unfused multi-wave is expressible. `_FakeDataType` (`:1594`) and `_kernel_dict` (`:1599`) let the bridge run with no real solution object. |
| Φ discharge (1649) | `gir/passes/tokens.py` | Fused reads await the **movement**, not a member; unfused awaits are byte-identical to a per-operand ledger; a fused instruction never carries the same await twice. |
| fence Mark (1793) | `gir/analyses/fence_regions.py` | Cross-agent-ness is the **agent count**, not the fuse — the two are separated by the two fixtures built for exactly that. |
| LdsHazards (1839) | `gir/analyses/lds_hazards.py` | Trip distance separates the failing cell from the passing ones; loop-carried read-after-write and write-after-read are both found; a same-agent edge needs no fence (*which is why a single-wave kernel needs no fence pass at all*); write-after-write is found at ring 1, the blind spot of the pre-existing conflict test; distinct rings do not alias; cross-block pairs are found rather than left to the block boundary; and every hazard is either token-visible or fence-separated. |
| fence cover (≈2001) | `fence_regions._admissible_slots`, `_cover`, `_separates` | A same-agent kernel gets **no** fences; **one** fence covers the whole steady body rather than one per edge; every cross-agent edge has a fence on **every** path between its ends (`paths`, `:2053`); and an undischargeable edge is an error, not a fence somewhere harmless (`_Bad`, `:2102`, with its `producer`/`consumer` stubs). |
| ShortPathFold (2119) | `gir/analyses/short_path.py`, `gir/passes/fold_short_path.py` | The fold compares **values**, not producer identities (`verdict`, `:2126`); the pass rewrites to the shared shape or keeps both arms (`_assert_fold_and_split_shapes`, `:2172`); and `_fold_matrix_cases` (`:2221`) plus `test_short_path_fold_is_decidable_for_every_known_hard_config` (`:2239`) run the decision over every configuration that has historically broken it. |
| ledger↔GIR differential (2272) | independent cross-check | `_ledger_shared_edges` (`:2278`) and `_gir_shared_edges` (`:2300`) derive the same edge set two ways and must agree — **and `test_the_ledger_gir_differential_can_actually_fail` (`:2341`) proves the differential is not vacuous**, which is the property most cross-checks lack. |
| LoopShape (2354) | `gir/analyses/loop_shape.py` | The test position is **derived** from where the branch sits (`_pre_tested_loop_prog`, `:2358`); the covering invariant holds and is enforced as `G-TRIP`; and the multi-copy case is pinned as *not yet expressible* rather than silently skipped. |
| model-only loudness (2466) | `gir/passes/record_unemitted.py`, `verify._check_emit` | A folded arm is **deleted**, not flagged; a kept arm is flagged with a recorded reason; the Marks a kept arm carries away are **counted**; `G-EMIT` fires both when the count is wrong and when the flag has no reason; and the recording pass refuses an undeclared flag rather than inventing one. `_fold_record` (`:2475`) and `_verify_error` (`:2480`) are the harness. |
| drain generation frame (2565) | `short_path._frame_base` | The drain's frame base is the **peel depth**, not zero, and the old base-zero frame is shown to fail the ring-depth rule — i.e. the test proves the old answer was wrong, not merely that the new one is self-consistent. |
| per-path `chunk_base` (2676) | `swap_regions._edge_delta`, `_unemitted_edges` | The folded entry edge carries the **arm's** frame, not the long path's; a folded configuration's entry edge is real dataflow; and **without** the per-path frame the folded join is unsolvable (`per_block_only`, `:2726`). A kept arm is the only thing excluded from the placement problem. |
| value_placement lattice (2787) | `gir/analyses/value_placement.py` | An ambiguous value **nobody consumes** is not a conflict — the case where two predecessors leave a register at different values with no downstream reader. `spy` (`:2793`) captures the conflict callback. |
| storage = (operand, region) (2824) | `lds_hazards._regions_of`, `_disjoint_storage` | A split tile's halves are storage-disjoint and raise no hazard; region awareness removes hazards **only** where there is a split; and an access that does not pin its region aliases **every** region. Stubs `_T` (`:2865`), `_R` (`:2869`), `acc` (`:2880`). |
| memory tokens (2900) | `gir/analyses/mem_tokens.py`, `verify._check_tokens` | Every logical buffer gets its own id; the ids **reach the emit plan**; every fence carries the ids of what it stands between; a fence names every buffer **live across** it, not just the edges that placed it; and `G-TOKEN` fires on an unnamed access or a token-less fence. |
| region walk (3078) | `gir/analyses/region_increment.py`, `walk_violations`, `verify._check_walk` | The descriptor steps between consecutive regions; the walk **closes** so the chunk stride stays plain; an unsplit movement emits no walk; each region is loaded once with its own token; and `G-WALK` fires when the walk is dropped, duplicated **or hoisted**. `_walked` (`:3071`) and `_walk` (`:3082`) extract it. |
| region as address (3157) | `emit_plan._plan_move`, `lds_geometry` | A split read carries **both** indices and they differ; an unsplit read has region 0 and the two agree; the region displacement is owed only by one of the two layouts; a packed split makes the inner coordinate **piecewise**; an unpacked split folds nothing; and the addresses are checked against a measured kernel (`addr`, `:3377`). |
| verify_dataflow (3586) | the five checkers | `_sweep_params` (`:3567`) drives the whole order × split × prefetch matrix to a clean plan; `_mutated` (`:3595`) then **injects each defect class by hand** and asserts the checker catches it — a region never read, a region the operand does not have, two generations sharing one register, a prologue priming too few substeps. |
| quantum (4390–4640) | `gir/quantum.py`, `refs.covered_coords` | The quantum defaults to one tile when nothing supplies it; a supplied quantum reaches the hop unchanged under every loop order; load and broadcast differ only in the **slot range**, with no tag; the carrier group is a **preimage**, so partners need not be adjacent; layer 3 obeys the supplied merge and invents none of its own; an incomplete carrier group is reported; the group check is **asymmetric** and the inference is why; and the two quantum faults are **labelled apart**. Stubs `_Act` (`:4556`, `:4603`, `:4650`), `viol` (`:4562`), `_P` (`:4646`). |
| render + meta (4680) | `gir/render.render_gir` | The dump shows the θ facts the blocks are derived from — added after a session in which a wrong conclusion survived because the facts were invisible. |
| Mma source coord (4749) | `loopir_to_gir._convert_mma` | An `Mma` source names **the operand's own** coordinate, not the WMMA grid, with two non-vacuity guards: an operand must actually be broadcast in this shape, and one source `Ref` must actually serve several instances. Stubs `_T` (`:4822`), `_R` (`:4825`), `_P` (`:4830`). |
| fused pairing (4789) | `region_increment._split_copies` | A fused movement's members are paired **by index**, and that is checked rather than assumed. |

The file's remaining local helpers are small extractors, listed once so the index is complete:
`_reaching` (`test_gir.py:33`), `_back_edges` (`:37`) and `_pending` (`:41`) each wrap one
`AnalysisManager().get(...)` call; `_as_tuple` (`:69`) normalizes a pointer identity;
`counts` (`:671`), `_counts` (`:3997`) and `_tokens_of` (`:2899`) aggregate acts or tokens;
`_units` (`:549`), `_boundaries` (`:1794`), `_hazards` (`:1843`), `_steady` (`:1848`),
`_fences` (`:1989`), `_slot_of` (`:2007`), `members` (`:2285`), `_gr_increments` (`:1399`),
`_read_acts` (`:3207`), `_read_plan` (`:3387`) and `_per_operand` (`:3432`) each project one kind of
result out of a built program; `_chain_prog` (`:1017`), `_tail_prog` (`:1224`), `_split_prog`
(`:2815`) and `_pre_tested_loop_prog` (`:2358`) hand-build CFGs; `_six_axis_words` (`:781`),
`_ord_of` (`:3721`), `_valid_loop_orders` (`:3741`), `_inner_word` (`:3849`), `_naming_helpers`
(`:3863`) and `grab` (`:3873`) drive the loop-order enumeration and the kernel-naming checks;
`seq` (`:1140`), `prologue` (`:1744`), `_fold_verdict` (`:2574`) and `numBytes` (`:1595`, `:3966`)
are one-liners.

##### 19.3.5 The other four suites

**`test_gir_to_rocisa.py` (29 tests)** covers the *pure* half of layer 3. `_finalized(params)`
(`:27`) lowers and runs the pipeline; `_kinds(actions)` (`:32`) projects the act kinds. What it
pins, beyond act counts and ordering: that `_plan_mma` picks the WMMA's two source slots via the
**derived** matmul-input list rather than by string comparison against `A`/`B`; that a multi-group
operand is **refused**; that `_register_depth` refuses divergent group widths within one operand;
that a ring deeper than the scaffold can name is refused; that `_append_tag` **appends and never
overwrites**; that `_wrap_lead` follows the closed form `lead = pf − min(to_chunk, M+1)`,
parametrized over seven `(M, to_chunk)` cells **and** cross-checked by an independent replay
(`test_wrap_lead_makes_every_stagger_start_cover_the_chunks_exactly_once`) that walks GIR's emitted
advance/copy sequence for every stagger start and asserts each chunk is covered exactly once; that
the prefetch index still matches the scaffold's own constant, *so a scaffold change fails here
rather than silently on hardware*; that a fence act reaches layer 3 carrying its must-set and scope;
that a single-wave kernel produces **no** fence act at all (not "layer 3 discards it" — the analysis
finds no cross-agent edge, so no Mark is ever made); that the retired discharge Mark survives in the
model and emits no instruction; and that the barrier strip keeps GIR fences and removes the
scaffold's.

**`test_value_placement.py` (11 tests)** is the sole test of `gir/analyses/value_placement.py`, and
it is the best-constructed suite in the package for one reason stated in its own header: the CFGs
are hand-built and **the answer is stated independently of the solver**, so a wrong fixpoint cannot
agree with the oracle by construction. `N` (`:22`) is a stand-in body node whose identity is what
the anchors compare; `_raise` (`:17`) is the conflict callback; `_pipeline(mod=2, adv=1)` (`:26`)
builds prologue → self-looping steady → drain with the back edge carrying the chunk advance. The
comment at `:41-44` is worth reading before changing the fixture: the latch's per-trip def runs
before the exit branch too, so the drain sits in the **post**-advance frame; giving the exit edge a
zero delta would model a drain that somehow missed the advance, and the solver would then correctly
report that one exit cannot serve two demands. What is pinned: that `meet` is a lattice and not a
preference (`meet(3, 4) is TOP`, never 3 or 4); that a self-looping rotating pointer's def lands at
the **end** of the body; the steady→drain hand-off; the diamond; and both sentinel anchors.

**`test_uniform_placement.py` (13 tests)** covers both layers of the same question, and its header
states the design rule the whole package should follow: *every test builds the **failing** shape
explicitly, because the passing case is the one the codebase already produces and a check that has
never been seen to fire is not a check.* `_fence(scope)` (`:23`) builds the Mark; `_two_block(...)`
(`:28`) builds a two-block program with the fence in the second, parametrized by block role,
predicate and metadata; `_run(prog)` (`:38`) runs the analysis; `_stream(inner_before_barrier)`
(`:126`) builds an instruction module shaped like the wave-parity stagger emitter — parity test,
skip branch, body, join label — and is the one helper that needs real instruction nodes. The GIR
half pins that a role-restricted block is a violation and so is a role-restricted **ancestor**; the
emission half pins that a selector inside a wave-parity arm is caught, that the same selector
hoisted above the parity test is accepted, that a **trip-count** arm does not count as
agent-discriminating, that a **backward** branch opens no region, and that only GIR-owned barriers
are judged.

**`test_tdm_split.py` (47 tests)** covers the pure geometry. Its header states the discipline: every
expectation is a **number read off an emitted kernel**, not a restatement of the implementation, and
it names the two reference shapes and their pass counts. The packed-versus-contiguous parametrization
is the clearest example — six cells over `(axis, unrollMajor)` establishing that it is a **diagonal**:
cutting the free axis of a free-major image is contiguous, cutting it in an unroll-major image is
packed, and the unroll axis is the mirror image. Both measured cells are in the table, including the
*negative* result where adding a region term regressed 82 passing kernels. The rest reproduces every
descriptor field for both layouts, the address arithmetic, the local-read fragment table with its
lane-interleave constant, and — via `region_derivation_check.TileCtx`/`check_tiles` — the agreement
between the tile-index and free-position derivations of a region.

##### 19.3.6 What the suite structurally cannot catch

This is the honest part. Six classes of defect are invisible to all 702 tests.

1. **Anything that requires the emitted assembly to be correct.** The suite checks the *plan*: which
   acts, in which order, with which indices and tokens. `leaves.py` — 773 lines, the largest single
   module after the lowering — has **no direct unit test**, because it imports the instruction
   extension at module scope. It is exercised only through whole-kernel emission comparison, which
   is not part of this suite. A wrong register name, a wrong offset immediate, a wrong instruction
   selection: all invisible here.
2. **Anything that requires hardware.** The three storage-split defect classes that motivated
   `verify_dataflow.py` were each found by running kernels and bisecting a pass/fail matrix. The
   checkers now catch *those*; they catch the next one only if it is expressible as a coordinate
   coverage property.

3. **The two offline tools are entirely untested.** `asm_lane_eval.py` (380 lines) and
   `lds_region_check.py` (315 lines) have no test and no in-tree caller. The all-zero degradation in
   `lanes_of` (§19.2.8, S2) is exactly the kind of defect a two-line test would have caught.
4. **Coarse invariants pass on fine-grained errors.** `G-OPERANDS` matches on `(operand, space)`, so
   "operand A is read somewhere" satisfies it even if the *specific* tile a given WMMA needs is
   never read. `check_register_dataflow` is the check that closes that, but it walks only
   `prologue` and `steady` (`check_plan` passes it the whole `plans` dict; only the two coverage
   checks are narrowed to `plans.get("steady")`), and its prologue live-in coverage is the open work
   item in §19.5.
5. **Inertness is invisible.** `UniformPlacement`'s two rules cannot fire on any program this
   lowering produces (§19.2.8, S8), yet `test_uniform_placement.py` passes 8 GIR-layer tests —
   because each hand-builds a program with a role-restricted block that `loopir_to_gir` never
   produces. The tests prove the *check* is correct; they say nothing about whether it is *reached*.
   The same caution applies to `_check_rotation_waw`: it is measured to have fired 0/1632 times.
6. **Nothing tests the pass pipeline's ordering constraints.** `pipeline()` returns a list, and the
   correctness of the *order* — CFG shaping strictly first, unemitted-Mark counting strictly last —
   is documented in the docstring and enforced by nothing. Reordering the list silently produces a
   program that verifies but whose analyses answered a different question. A cheap improvement:
   assert in `run_pipeline` that no `StructuralPass` appears after a non-structural one.

A seventh, milder gap: **the renderer is not round-trip checked**. `render_gir` (`gir/render.py:304`)
and `gir_counts` (`:348`) produce a debug view, and the module docstring explicitly *retracts* a
prior claim that a round-trip check existed over that text. The parity that is checked runs on
`gir_counts` and on the emit plan's acts, never on the rendered strings. Two tests
(`test_gir.py:4670` and a pair in `test_loopmodel.py`) assert specific lines appear, and that is all.
`gir_counts` (`gir/render.py:348`) does count model-only blocks' operations, deliberately — the
per-block dict carries a `model_only` boolean beside the three counters so a consumer comparing
against the emitted assembly can subtract, while a consumer comparing against the layer-1 tree wants
every operation GIR holds. Nothing forces a caller to read the flag.

---

#### 19.4 Extension recipes

Each recipe names every file and symbol that must change. They are ordered from most local to most
invasive.

##### 19.4.1 Adding a terminator kind

Four sites, and three of them are duplicates that should be collapsed first.

1. Define the dataclass in `gir/nodes.py`, next to the other terminators (`Goto` `:229`, `CondGoto`
   `:235`, `Trips` `:248`, `LoopBack` `:279`, `Return` `:296`, `CondChain` `:309`). Give it a
   `render()` if it carries a predicate, and a `__post_init__` if any field combination is invalid —
   `CondChain.__post_init__` (`:331`) is the model.
2. Add it to **`successor_labels(blk)`** (`gir/nodes.py:342`). This is *the* authority. Return
   targets in program-significant order and do **not** filter against `prog.blocks` — the caller
   decides whether to drop the `"end"` pseudo-target.
3. Add it to the three copies of that switch: `verify._term_targets` (`gir/verify.py:337`),
   `fold_short_path._targets` (`gir/passes/fold_short_path.py:197`) and `early_exit._targets`
   (`gir/passes/early_exit.py:112`). **Better: delete all three and call `successor_labels`.** They
   exist only because each predates the extraction, and the two pass-local copies already do not
   handle `Return`. Neither pass currently runs on a program containing one, so the bug is latent —
   but a future one will.
4. Export it from `gir/__init__.py`. Note the existing inconsistency: `gir/__init__.py:12` imports
   `Trips` and `LoopBack` but the terminator row of `__all__` (`:33`) omits both. They are
   importable and the tests import them from `gir.nodes` directly, but they are not advertised.
   Fix that while you are there.

Then: add a test in the `test_gir.py` control-flow band (the `CondChain` block at `:1014`, the
`Return` block at `:1176` and the tail-loop block at `:1220` are three worked examples, each pinning
construction, verification, rendering, dominance survival, and a rejected malformed case).

##### 19.4.2 Adding an analysis

The contract is short: **an `Analysis` is pure**. It reads `prog`, may demand other analyses through
`am`, and returns a result object. It must not mutate anything reachable from `prog`.

1. Create `gir/analyses/<name>.py`. Import from `..nodes`, `..refs`, `..analysis` and sibling
   analyses only — **never** from `..passes`, never from `rocisa`, and (with the single existing
   exception at `gir/analyses/dep_defuse.py:19`) never upward into layer 1.
2. Subclass `Analysis` (`gir/analysis.py:24`) and implement `run(self, prog, am)`
   (`gir/analysis.py:36`). Override the `cache_key` property (`:32`) **only** if the analysis is
   parameterized, or if you want a stable name that survives a class rename — the three existing
   overrides (`dep_defuse.py:45`, `reg_band.py:40`, `gr_increment.py:119`) are all the latter, and
   are no-ops in effect today.
3. Return a **result object with a query API**, not a bare dict. `LdsHazardSet`
   (`gir/analyses/lds_hazards.py:145`), `MemTokenSet` (`gir/analyses/mem_tokens.py:82`), `RegBand`
   (`gir/analyses/reg_band.py:27`) and `BackEdgeSet` (`gir/analyses/cfg.py:69`) are the pattern. The
   reason is concrete: a bare dict forces every consumer to re-derive the grouping rule and to key on
   `id(node)`, which is how three modules ended up with three different answers to "which operand
   does this shared hop belong to" before `refs.copy_unit` was extracted.
4. If the analysis can fail to answer for some inputs, expose the gaps as a **named property**
   (`MemTokenSet.unresolved`, `LdsHazardSet.unresolved()`) *and wire a verifier clause to it*. The
   second half is the one that gets skipped — see §19.2.8, S3.
5. Export from `gir/analyses/__init__.py`, and decide explicitly whether it also belongs in
   `gir/__init__.py`. Twenty-four names currently live only in the inner list, including three whole
   subsystems that `verify_gir` itself calls; that is accretion, not policy, so copying the omission
   is not a decision.

##### 19.4.3 Adding a pass

First decide **which kind**, because the base classes encode two different contracts
(`gir/passes/base.py`).

- **`Pass`** (`gir/passes/base.py:15`, `structural = False` at `:22`) may edit block *bodies* —
  insert or remove instructions — but the block set, the terminators and the `preds`/`succs` lists
  must be identical on the way out. `structural = False` is a **claim the pass makes**, not a
  restriction the runtime enforces.
- **`StructuralPass`** (`gir/passes/base.py:33`, `structural = True` at `:61`) may change the CFG:
  add or remove blocks, retarget terminators, move the loop test. Its contract, from the docstring:
  (i) leave `preds`/`succs` agreeing with every terminator — **including for blocks it did not touch
  but whose predecessor set it changed**; (ii) leave the program passing `verify_gir`, in particular
  the reduction-coverage invariant, so a pass that rotates a loop or changes its trip count cannot
  quietly move the total work; (iii) call `prog.bump()`. What it may **not** do is change what the
  kernel computes: moving instructions between blocks is allowed, adding or dropping a `Move`/`Mma`
  is a model change and belongs in θ.

The distinction is a *type* rather than a convention because it was once only a comment.
`ApplyMarksPass` described itself as "the only IR mutator" for a long time; the short-arm folding
pass made that false when it started deleting blocks, and nothing noticed. There are three structural
passes today, and all three run: `ScaffoldShapePass` (`gir/passes/scaffold_shape.py:47`, the one
CFG-shaping stage in the pipeline) and the two it composes, `FoldShortPathPass` and
`EarlyExitPass` — the latter retargets terminators and builds `CondChain` arms, so it owes the
same preds/succs + `verify_gir` + `prog.bump()` contract. The queued ones are loop rotation and
critical-edge splitting.

Then:

1. Implement `run(self, prog, am)` (`gir/passes/base.py:28`), returning an iterable of invalidated
   analysis names — `()` if the pass mutates nothing. `name` (`:25`) defaults to the class name.
2. **If the pass mutates, call `prog.bump()`.** `run_pipeline` also clears the manager after every
   pass, but a pass run directly (as several tests do) has only the bump.
3. Add it to `pipeline()` (`gir/passes/pipeline.py:36`) at the right position. The two hard ordering
   constraints: **every CFG-shaping stage must precede everything else** (every later stage is an
   *analysis over that CFG*, and an edge added afterwards does not make those analyses wrong, it
   makes them answers to a different question with nothing able to detect the difference), and
   **`RecordUnemittedPass` must stay last**, because it counts Marks that arrive mid-pipeline —
   counting at fold time reported zero.
4. Export from `gir/passes/__init__.py`.

If your pass produces `Mark`s, do **not** insert them. Produce `PendingMark`s
(`gir/region.py:59`) from an analysis, register that analysis in
`CollectPendingMarksPass.__init__`'s default list (`gir/passes/collect_pending.py:25` — the
constructor takes a `region_analyses` override precisely so this is extensible), and let
`PlacementPass` and `ApplyMarksPass` do the rest. Choose the `Region`'s policy
(`gir/region.py:31-32`) by *what the Mark mutates*: `EARLIEST` for anything feeding a load
descriptor (every cycle between the update and the load it feeds is overlap), `MIDPOINT` for the LDS
read pointer (bounded by two *different* resources, so it must not be slammed to either edge). There
is no third policy and no `PINNED`: a fence's window is a *degenerate* one-slot `Region` built by
`fence_regions._region_at` (`gir/analyses/fence_regions.py:247`) carrying the default `EARLIEST`,
which on a one-slot window resolves to that slot. Searching for a `PINNED` symbol finds only prose.

##### 19.4.4 Adding a checker

Two homes, and picking the wrong one is the common mistake.

- **A shape invariant** — something that must hold of any well-formed `Program`, checkable without
  knowing the GEMM. Add a `_check_<name>(prog)` (or `(prog, am)`) to `gir/verify.py`, raise
  `GirVerifyError` with a `G-<NAME>:` prefix, and add the call to `verify_gir`
  (`gir/verify.py:422`) in the right position — earlier if it localizes better, later if it is
  expensive or depends on an analysis.
  **Before you do:** confirm it holds *mid-pipeline* and on raw `lower_to_gir` output, because
  `verify_gir` is called in both places. If it only holds of the finished program, it belongs at the
  tail of `run_pipeline` next to `_check_rotation_waw` (`gir/passes/pipeline.py:74`) instead. This is
  not hypothetical: putting the rotation write-after-write check in `verify_gir` failed 448 of 948
  tests, all of them for that reason.
- **A semantic property** — "does this plan compute the right GEMM?" Add a
  `check_<name>(prog, acts=None) -> list[str]` to `gir/verify_dataflow.py`, **return** violations
  rather than raising, add it to `check_plan` (`gir/verify_dataflow.py:277`), and export it from
  `gir/__init__.py`. Returning a list is what lets the same function serve a report-only matrix
  sweep and a hard build gate.

Write the violation message so it names the *shape*, not just the fact. Compare the two styles:
`"a region is not read"` versus the actual text, which prints the operand, both source coordinates,
the address key they collided on, whether the split is packed or contiguous, and therefore which
coordinates the address is built from. The second turns a bisect into a read.

And **build the failing case in the test**, per the rule `test_uniform_placement.py` states in its
header. `test_gir.py`'s `_mutated` (`:3595`) is the worked example: it takes a good plan and injects
each defect class by hand — a region never read, a region the operand does not have, two generations
sharing one register, a prologue priming too few substeps — then asserts the checker catches each.
A checker that has only ever been run on correct input is not a checker.

##### 19.4.5 Adding an instruction or a data type at the leaf layer

This is the recipe with the most external dependencies, because `leaves.py` is where the package
stops being self-contained.

1. **Find the refusal that fires.** Run the configuration; the `NotImplementedError` message names
   the parameter. The refusal table in §19.2.7 maps each message to its line.
2. **Decide whether it is a widening or a new path.** The distinction is made explicitly in the
   source and it matters. Bytes-per-element 1 and 2 share one read path with one fragment table;
   the sub-byte formats do **not** — they have a different register packing, a padded register
   stride, and a per-load register count that is not the block width (`leaves.py:478-483`). Widening
   the accepted set without adding the branch produces plausible, wrong assembly. The same applies
   to the non-square matrix instruction (`leaves.py:518-526`): it needs an extra per-tile
   displacement term the fragment table does not have.
3. **If the change is arithmetic, it goes in `lds_geometry.py`, not in `leaves.py`.** That module
   imports nothing from the project and is unit-tested without the instruction extension. The
   fragment table is `read_fragments` (`lds_geometry.py:33`), and it **raises** on a shape it cannot
   tile — which is the honest answer, because the alternative is a register span the WMMA then reads
   unwritten. Its two invariants are worth restating: the fragments must tile the tile's registers
   exactly (no gap, no overlap), and they must cover the instruction's whole reduction extent given
   the lane interleave.
4. **Add the acceptance test in `test_tdm_split.py`**, in the style that file mandates: the expected
   value is a **number read off an emitted kernel**, with the kernel named in the docstring. Do not
   restate the formula.
5. **Then, and only then, touch `leaves.py`.** Add the branch, keep the refusal for everything
   outside it, and remember that the three `build*Context` methods (`buildMfmaContext`
   `leaves.py:164`, `buildMxScaleReadContext` `:364`, `buildLdsReadContext` `:462`) are constructed
   **once per kernel** and are loop-order-invariant by contract — anything that varies per act
   belongs in the emitter (`emitWmmaTile` `:245`, `emitLdsReadTile` `:611`, `emitCopyTile` `:745`),
   not in the context.
6. If a new accumulator type is involved, extend the table in `_abbrevToInstType`
   (`leaves.py:126`). It deliberately covers only the accumulator side; the input side reads the
   shared 40-way dtype-pair table the scaffold already owns, which is why mixed 8-bit float pairs
   need no change here.

##### 19.4.6 Adding an operand (a new tensor role)

The good news: **`operand` is an open string set everywhere in `gir/`**, and there is no role
vocabulary to extend. `Mma.srcs` (`gir/nodes.py:133`) is a flat tuple and which source is a matmul
input, which is a scale and which is metadata is read off `Ref.tile.operand` and off θ's
`meta['mma_inputs']`. A plain kernel has two sources, a microscaling kernel four, a sparse one
three. Adding a fifth needs no node change.

What it does need, in order:

1. **θ must emit it.** The operand, its presence (which iteration modes it varies over), its ring
   depth and its register rotation width all come from layer 1. GIR consumes and validates; it never
   invents. This is the bulk of the work and it is outside this package.
2. **`meta` must carry the facts about it.** The keys that are per-operand maps and therefore need an
   entry: `operand_regions`, `region_modes`, `region_agent_relative`, `agent_distributed`,
   `read_quantum`, `quantum_axes`. `unit_regions` is keyed by *movement*, so a fused member needs an
   entry there instead. If the operand is a matmul input, `mma_inputs` changes too.
3. **Decide its pairing.** If it is a *scale-like* operand that must follow a parent, `_plan_mma`
   (`gir/emit_plan.py:193`) pairs it by **free-mode presence**: the extra source's free-mode set must
   equal exactly one matmul input's, and it refuses at `:233` when it matches zero or two. That is
   the whole pairing rule — there is no name literal, and adding one would be a regression. If your
   operand's presence does not distinguish it, that is a θ problem, not a plan problem.
4. **Give it a read leaf** if it reads from LDS with a different geometry. `buildMxScaleReadContext`
   (`leaves.py:364`) is the worked example for a whole second read shape: it derives the parent's
   block size *from the tensor char* (`mxTc = tc[3]`, `leaves.py:412`) rather than taking it as an
   argument, so a caller cannot pair a scale tensor with the wrong parent's block size — copy that
   discipline.
5. **Check the four coverage properties still hold.** Run the matrix sweep in `test_gir.py`
   (`_sweep_params`, `:3567`) and `check_plan`; a new operand that is not covered by
   `check_source_coverage` because θ gave it no source coordinate will pass silently.
6. **Add a fixture** in `gir_fixtures.py` if the operand introduces a new *shape* rather than a new
   name, following the one-key-delta rule.

##### 19.4.7 Adding a Mark kind

Rarely needed, but the closed set is deliberate and the process is short.

1. Add the name to `MARK_KINDS` (`gir/nodes.py:157`) — it is a closed tuple of six today:
   `phase_boundary`, `fence`, `swap`, `gr_increment`, `region_increment`, `gsu_guard`.
2. Add its required `at` keys to `_MARK_SCHEMA` (`gir/verify.py:75`). If a required key depends on
   the *value* of another key, the schema cannot express it and you must add a special case in
   `_check_marks` — `swap`'s hop-dependent pointer key (`gir/verify.py:410`) is the precedent.
3. Add a `_plan_mark` case (`gir/emit_plan.py:274`) naming the payload the act carries, and a
   dispatch arm in `GirToRocisa.emit_block` (`gir_to_rocisa.py:110`).
4. **Do not name it after its realization.** There is no `barrier` kind and never was: GIR carries
   the *ordering obligation*, and whether it becomes a barrier instruction, a wait-count, or nothing
   at all is the backend's decision from the target configuration. On the path where the downstream
   scheduler re-derives every barrier, a GIR-emitted one would be discarded, so presuming the
   realization in the node name would have been wrong on that path. (The comment above the tuple
   still says "`await` replaces the never-created `barrier` kind", but the kind is spelled `fence`
   and `await` appears nowhere — the reasoning is right, the word is one rename behind.)

##### 19.4.8 Teaching the offline tools a new opcode

The two sidecar modules of §18.3 and §18.4 — `asm_lane_eval.py` (380 L) and `lds_region_check.py`
(315 L) — are 695 lines with **no unit tests and no in-tree callers** (§19.3.1 records this, and
§18.4.6 item 4 explains why it is tolerable). That combination makes them the one part of the
package where a recipe genuinely matters: nothing will tell you that you got it wrong.

**The failure you will hit first.** `LaneEval.step` (`asm_lane_eval.py:261`) ends in
`raise UnsupportedInstruction(op)` (`:376`), so the tool stops with the mnemonic the moment the
emitter grows an instruction it does not model. That is the design, stated at the top of the file
(`:21`): *refusal is the point*, because the alternative — skipping the instruction — leaves a
register holding a stale value and produces a confidently wrong address. So the workflow below is
not optional maintenance; it is what running the tool on a new kernel *is*.

1. **Read the mnemonic off the exception**, then find the instruction in the emitted `.s` and note
   its real operand order. This is where the mistakes are: several gfx1250 forms are `REV`
   (`v_lshlrev_b32`'s shift amount is *src0*, see the comment at `:166`), several are
   three-address fused forms (`v_lshl_add_u32` = `(s0 << s1) + s2`), and a compare's destination
   is parsed as its first *source*.
2. **Pick the right table — do not add an `if` in `step` unless you must.** The tables *are* the
   semantics, deliberately, so that no per-opcode dispatch method can drift from them:
   - `_BIN` (`:157`) — two-source pure functions of lane values, the common case. One line.
   - `_UN` (`:85`) — one-source scalar functions.
   - `_BIN2` (`:96`) — two-source *scalar* functions (`s_min_u32`, `s_bfm_b32`, …).
   - `_CMP` (`:178`) — VGPR compares; these write `self.vcc`, not a register.
   - `_SCC_CMP` (`:91`) — scalar compares; these write `self.scc`, which exists solely because
     `s_cselect_b32` selects the split path's wave-parity value and guessing it would pick the
     wrong region.
   - `_BFE` (`:108`) — the bit-field-extract pair, whose src1 packs offset and width.
   An explicit arm in `step` is correct only when the opcode is not a pure function of its
   sources: a kernarg load (`s_load_bN`, `:310`), a 64-bit pair op (`_step64`, `:239`), a float
   op (`_stepf`, `:202`), or anything that reads `vcc`/`scc`.
3. **64-bit and float go in their own handlers, and the reason is not stylistic.** An operand is
   parsed as its *first* register, so the high half of a pair is implicit at `idx + 1` — collapsing
   `s_mov_b64` into a 32-bit move leaves the high register holding a stale value that a later
   `s_add_u64` folds into an address (`:239-242` says exactly this). Floats are modelled as real
   IEEE bit patterns rather than Python floats (`_f32`/`_b32`/`_f64`/`_b64`, `:194-200`) because
   the integer-divide sequence writes a value as float and reads it back as bits at both ends.
4. **If your opcode is an approximation in hardware, do not model it exactly and stop there.**
   `v_rcp_*` is the precedent: `LaneEval` computes the exact reciprocal, and `check` compensates by
   **re-running the whole slice with a perturbed reciprocal** and refusing if the two runs disagree
   on any address (`:192-193`, and §18.4.5). Any new approximate opcode needs the same treatment —
   an exact model plus a perturbation run — or it silently converts a hardware rounding difference
   into a clean bill of health.
5. **Never widen `read`.** `read` (`:110`) raises on an unwritten register on purpose, and the
   docstring records the incident: reading unwritten state as zero once produced "ZERO VIOLATIONS
   for four kernels", a clean bill of health manufactured entirely from uninitialized registers.
   If your new opcode's source is a kernel input, seed it through the `kernarg=` dict or the
   caller's seed arguments — do not add a default. (`lanes_of` at `:379` *does* default to zeros
   and is the one place this discipline is already broken; it is S2 in §19.2.8 and should be fixed
   before it is imitated.)
6. **On the `lds_region_check.py` side**, a new *instruction shape* (not just a new mnemonic) may
   also need `parse_instructions` (`:183`) to extract its destination and width correctly. Check
   `_operand_width` (`:179`) in particular: a def of a register range defines *every* register in
   it, and under-claiming that width is the documented bug that made a lane-local address appear
   to depend on kernarg-loaded problem sizes (S15 in §19.2.8).
7. **Then write the test that does not exist.** There is no test module for either file, so the
   honest minimum for any change here is a `Tests/unit/` file with (a) one hand-written assembly
   fragment per opcode you added, asserting the lane values, and (b) one negative control that
   feeds an unmodelled mnemonic and asserts `UnsupportedInstruction`. Item (b) is the important
   one: it is what keeps the refusal discipline from being quietly removed later. Adding that file
   is also the cheapest way to retire §18.4.6 item 4.

#### 19.5 Known gaps and deferred work

Each entry states the gap, where it is recorded in the source, what currently happens, and what
closing it would take. They are grouped by whether they are *unmodelled* (GIR has nothing to say),
*unrealized* (GIR says it, layer 3 cannot emit it) or *unchecked* (nothing enforces a claim).

##### 19.5.1 Unmodelled — the model does not cover it

**G1. The write/store side and the epilogue.** GIR models the *read* trajectory
`global → shared → register → compute`. The accumulator-to-global path is absent entirely: no node,
no analysis, no verifier clause. Two consequences. First, the single-LDS-buffer configuration (where
the same LDS is reused for the epilogue's data staging) cannot be reasoned about, because the
epilogue's writes are invisible to `LdsHazards` and to `MemTokenAssignment`, so a write-after-read on
the reused space cannot be found. Second, the ring-1 copy in GIR carries no write-after-read edge at
all. *Closing it* means: a `Move` with `dsts` in `global` space; a hazard kind for
register-lifetime-vs-store; an operand for the destination tensor with its own presence; and a phase
after `drain{M-1}`. It is comparable in size to the read side.

**G2. The tail loop and the edge cases.** When the reduction extent is not a whole multiple of the
chunk size, or the free extents are not whole multiples of the macro tile, the pre-existing kernel
scaffold emits additional loop and guard structure. GIR has a `'tail'` phase in its block-phase
domain (`gir/nodes.py:373`) and `_check_cfg` accepts a tail loop as a legitimate second loop region
(`gir/verify.py:204`), but nothing *produces* one: the lowering emits no tail block, and the
scaffold serves the remainder itself. So the tail's reads, copies and pointer state are outside the
model. *Closing it* needs a per-level peel treatment for a runtime-extent chunk — the harder half is
that the drain and the tail overlap in the storage-split configurations, where the reduction-axis
split's remainder collides with the tail while the free-axis split's does not.

**G3. Wave specialization / role-restricted blocks.** `Block.role` (`gir/nodes.py`) is `'all'`
everywhere, and neither `Pred` nor `Bound` can spell an agent-discriminating guard (`Bound` is
`var + const` and `Pred` is `counter op bound`). Consequently `UniformPlacement`'s two rules —
"a proc-scoped fence in a role-restricted block is a violation" and "a fence under an
agent-discriminating predicate is a violation" — are **structurally inert**
(`gir/analyses/uniform_placement.py:38-45`). *Closing it* needs a role vocabulary, a predicate form
that can name an agent identity, and the lowering to produce them. Until then, all shipped safety on
this question comes from the emission-layer text scan.

**G4. A persistent / grid-stride outer loop.** `verify_gir`'s `expect_steady_loops="ge1"` argument
exists for it (`gir/verify.py:422`) and nothing else does. The CFG shape is expressible; the frame
arithmetic (`chunk_base` across an outer trip) is not worked out.

**G5. Narrowing an agent-relative read to the region it actually touches.** An operand flagged
`region_agent_relative` gets **every** region's token, because the producers of the regions it does
not name would otherwise go unordered (`gir/analyses/mem_tokens.py:157`). That is *sound* and it is
*imprecise*: a single wave touches one region, so the read is ordered against producers it cannot
alias. The residual gap is exactness, not expressibility — the agent fact is already modelled. The
cost is extra ordering, never a wrong answer.

##### 19.5.2 Unrealized — GIR expresses it, layer 3 refuses it

**U1. Register partitions (several register groups per operand).** Three refusals guard it:
`_plan_mma` at `gir/emit_plan.py:253` (the plan carries one slot per operand), `_register_depth` at
`gir_to_rocisa.py:65` (the leaf's fallback takes one scalar W per operand), and the leaf's own
addressing. `RegBandAnalysis` **already computes** the per-`(operand, group)` widths
(`gir/analyses/reg_band.py:43`) and `RegBand.width(operand, group)` (`:31`) already answers the
per-group question — the map exists and nothing consumes it. *Closing it* means: make the emit plan
carry a per-group slot list instead of a scalar `bufA`/`bufB`; make `_register_depth` return the
`(operand, group)` map unchanged; and teach the WMMA leaf to select the group. The shape that needs
it is an operand whose two halves rotate at different widths (one rotating a 2-deep ring, one
in-place), which is a real microscaling configuration.

**U2. A region step across several axes at once.** `gir_to_rocisa.py:211`. GIR carries a per-axis
step vector; the descriptor primitive walks one axis per call, and the flat `steps` scalar is only a
byte displacement while a single axis is live. The current parameter domain cannot produce a
two-axis step, so this is latent. *Closing it* is one add per non-zero axis with that axis's own
stride — the information is already on the Mark (`axis_steps`).

**U3. A multi-chunk global-read advance.** `gir_to_rocisa.py:434`. The scaffold's increment emits
exactly one chunk stride. *Closing it* needs a scaled increment on the scaffold side.

**U4. A fused movement outside the aliased pairs.** `gir_to_rocisa.py:371`. The scaffold aliases one
descriptor per pair at multiple waves; a cross-pair group, or any fuse at a single wave, has no
emitter.

**U5. The split-U guard.** `gsu_guard` is in the closed Mark set, `_plan_mark` can plan it, and
`gir_to_rocisa.py:220` is a `pass`. Nothing produces it. See §19.2.8 S9 for the sharp edge.

##### 19.5.3 Unchecked — a claim nothing enforces

**C1. `LdsHazardSet.unresolved()` has no production reader** (§19.2.8, S3). One verifier clause
closes it.

**C2. `check_address_keys` is not in `check_plan`** (`gir/verify_dataflow.py:230`). It catches a real
defect class — a packed split whose address is built from flat coordinates — and it runs only in
tests. Wiring it needs a `packed` predicate from the caller, because the rule lives in
`lds_geometry.region_split_is_packed` (`lds_geometry.py:94`) and `gir/` may not import it. The clean
form is a callable parameter on `check_plan`, following the same precedent the movement-quantum
plumbing already uses.

**C3. Nothing checks that two analyses do not place conflicting Marks in the same window.** The
three-layer insertion model (§4.1) buys purity, cacheability and a one-line policy change; it does
**not** buy conflict detection. Two `PendingMark`s whose Regions overlap are simply both inserted,
in an order determined by `sorted(insertions, key=..., reverse=True)`
(`gir/passes/apply_marks.py:39`) — i.e. by body index, with ties broken by insertion order into the
list. This is the obvious next invariant.

**C4. Nothing checks that a `Region`'s anchors are in the block the `Region` names.** §19.2.8, S1
and S12.

**C5. Nothing checks the pass order.** §19.3.6, item 6.

**C6. The multi-block steady chain over-covers the reduction, unchecked.** §19.2.8, S4.

**C7. `check_register_dataflow`'s prologue coverage.** The steady body's upward-exposed uses — the
registers it reads on its *first* trip, before it has written them — must be covered by the
prologue's defs. The checker walks the plan and models the loop-carried edge, but the live-in
coverage across the prologue→steady boundary is the piece still being finished.

#### 19.6 Cost, complexity, and where to look if compilation gets slow

Everything in this package runs **once per kernel**, in pure Python, at code-generation time. The
whole stack is built once and cached (`KernelWriter.py:3776`, keyed on kernel name), and the three
phase forks then only *ask the emitter for their block* — that build-once property is what keeps the
cost linear in kernels rather than in kernels × phases.

Let *V* be blocks, *E* edges, *N* body instructions per block, *A* shared accesses per block, *S* the
ring depth, *M* the peel depth. Practical values, from the shipping configurations: **V = 4 to 12**
(one prologue, one or two steady, `M` drains, up to `M` short), **E ≈ 2V**, **N = 20 to 200**,
**A = 4 to 40**, **S ∈ {1, 2, 3}**, **M ∈ {1, 2, 3}**.

| component | complexity | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Program.walk_rpo` (`gir/nodes.py:487`) | O(V + E) | Recursive post-order with an on-stack set, then reversed. Every CFG walk in the package is at this scale. |
| `Dominators` (`gir/analyses/cfg.py:23`) | O(V²·E) worst case for the classic iterative set formulation | At V ≤ 12 this is microseconds. Do not replace it with a Lengauer–Tarjan until V is in the hundreds. |
| `GenReaching` (`gir/analyses/gen_reaching.py:114`) | O((V + E)·|Gen|) | The transfer function is nine lines; the SSA value class is a single integer generation. |
| **`LdsHazards`** (`gir/analyses/lds_hazards.py:329`) | **O(V·A² + V²·A²)** | The dominant cost. Same-block pairing is O(A²) per block (`:342`); `_cross_block` (`:345`) is a full O(V²) block-pair loop with an O(A²) inner product. At V = 12, A = 40 that is ~230k `_pair`/`_kind` calls — still milliseconds, but it is the only quadratic-in-two-things term in the package. |
| `FenceRegions` greedy cover (`gir/analyses/fence_regions.py:75`) | O(H · N) per block for admissibility, then O(H · N) per greedy round, ≤ H rounds | H = cross-agent hazards, typically < 10. `_separates` (`:161`) does a graph reachability per query, O(V + E) each. |
| `ValuePlacementSolver` (`gir/analyses/value_placement.py:92`) | Two fixpoints, each O(V · E) iterations × O(A) per block | Run once per `(hop, unit)` and once per movement, so a constant number of times. |
| `ShortPathFold` (`gir/analyses/short_path.py:398`) | O(M · N) to simulate both arms, plus O(consumers) to compare | Linear. |
| `emit_plan.plan_block` (`gir/emit_plan.py:296`) | O(N · modes) | `_project` (`:62`) is a mixed-radix fold over the mode set. |
| `check_plan` (`gir/verify_dataflow.py:277`) | O(acts · registers) | Explicitly cheap by design — it is the gate that runs on every kernel. |
| `uniform_emission.check_uniform_placement` (`uniform_emission.py:214`) | O(I) to flatten and label, O(I) to find regions with a `_LOOKBACK`-bounded backscan, then O(barriers × regions) | I ≈ 1750 emitted items through the main loop. The final product is the only super-linear term and both factors are small (measured: 8540 regions and 4053 barriers across **5028** kernels, i.e. ~1.7 regions and ~0.8 barriers per kernel). |

**Where the compile-time cost actually sits, and what to do about it.** Nothing in this package is
currently a bottleneck — a whole kernel's lowering, pipeline, verification and planning is
milliseconds against a code-generation step measured in seconds. If that changes, the order to look
in is:

1. **`AnalysisManager` invalidation granularity** (`gir/analysis.py:55`). `run_pipeline` clears the
   entire cache after **every** pass (`gir/passes/pipeline.py:67`), so `Dominators`, `BackEdges` and
   `GenReaching` are recomputed after a pass that touched only bodies. The machinery to fix it
   already exists and is unused: `Pass.run` returns the invalidated names, `ApplyMarksPass` returns
   `("body",)`, `TokensPass` returns `("tokens",)`, and `invalidate(names)` accepts and ignores them.
   Wiring those three together is the single highest-value change here, and it is maybe twenty lines.
   The reason it has not been done is that the numbers do not justify it at V ≤ 12.
2. **`LdsHazards._cross_block`'s O(V²) block-pair loop** (`gir/analyses/lds_hazards.py:345`). It
   already prunes on reachability (`cb not in reachable.get(pb, ())`) before the inner product, which
   is what keeps it tractable. The next prune, if needed, is to bucket accesses by
   `(operand, region)` *before* pairing, since `_disjoint_storage` (`:267`) rejects most pairs
   immediately — that turns O(A²) into O(Σ A_b²) over storage buckets, which for a split operand is
   a factor of `nsplit` and for a two-operand kernel a factor of four.
3. **Precompute `_shared_accesses` once.** `LdsHazards` builds `by_block` (`:337`) and
   `mem_tokens.shared_refs` (`gir/analyses/mem_tokens.py:115`) walks the same structure again for the
   same purpose. Their docstrings acknowledge the duplication — one builds the richer `Access` record
   the hazard pairing needs, the other only has to reach every `Ref` — but a single walk producing
   both views would be strictly better and is a contained change.
4. **`_separates` recomputes reachability per query** (`gir/analyses/fence_regions.py:161`). It
   deletes the candidate block and re-asks whether the consumer is still reachable from the producer.
   That predicate is *correct* — it subsumes reachability, dominance and the self-loop special case
   in one test, which is why it replaced an existential-reachability version that got the multi-block
   case wrong — but it is O(V + E) per call and it is called once per (hazard, candidate) pair.
   Caching per candidate block is trivial if it ever matters.
5. **Do not** "optimize" `Dominators` or `walk_rpo`. They are O(V)-ish on a graph with a dozen nodes
   and are not measurable.

One non-obvious cost that is **not** in this package but is caused by it: the build-once cache is
keyed on kernel *name* (`KernelWriter.py:3779`), with `id(kernel)` as a fallback. If two kernels ever
share a name, the second silently reuses the first's program. That has not happened, and the name is
supposed to be unique by construction, but it is a single-entry cache (`cache[0] == key`), so it also
means an interleaved emission of two kernels rebuilds each time.
