and they are also the two with the worst asymptotics in the package. That is not a contradiction: it
is `P = 20` marks against `L = 387`, and `20 × 387` is small. It becomes interesting only if the
number of marks ever grows with the body — which is exactly what a per-obligation fence design would
have done, and is the shape a future `gsu_guard` or per-region await could reintroduce.

`PlacementPass.run` (`gir/passes/placement.py:31`) resolves every `PendingMark`'s `Region` to an
anchor. `_resolve(prog, region)` (`:37`) calls `_slot(body, anchor, opening)` (`:47`) twice, and
`_slot` is **a linear scan of the body comparing node identity** (`for i, node in enumerate(body): if
node is anchor`). So placement is `O(P · L)`. The `MIDPOINT` policy then picks `lo + (hi−lo)//2` and
`EARLIEST` picks `lo`; a malformed window (`hi < lo`) falls back to the stated `before` bound rather
than raising.

`ApplyMarksPass.run` (`gir/passes/apply_marks.py:20`) groups the placed marks by block, resolves each
anchor with `_anchor_index(body, anchor)` (`:45`) — **the same linear identity scan** — and then
inserts back-to-front by index so earlier insertions do not shift later anchors. Two costs stack:
`O(P · L)` for the scans and `O(P · L)` for the `list.insert` shifts. It clears `prog.pending` and
calls `prog.bump()`, and returns `("body",)` — an invalidation hint nothing consumes.

The fix, if it is ever needed, is one dictionary: build `{id(node): index}` once per block before
resolving that block's marks, turning both passes into `O(P + L)`. It is deliberately *not* done
today, and the reason is a real design property rather than laziness: a `Region`'s anchors are
**opaque node references, not indices**, precisely so that a Region computed by one analysis survives
another analysis's Marks being inserted into the same body before it is resolved. An index map is
compatible with that (build it after all marks are collected, which is where both passes already
sit), but it must be rebuilt per block and invalidated on any insertion — so the map has to be built
in `ApplyMarksPass` *before* the insert loop begins, not incrementally.

`CollectPendingMarksPass` (`gir/passes/collect_pending.py:24`, `__init__` at `:25`, `run` at `:31`)
is a four-line driver: run the four region analyses through the manager, concatenate their
`PendingMark` lists onto `prog.pending`, mutate nothing. Its 65 ms is entirely its callees. The
constructor takes an optional analysis list, which is how a test exercises one region analysis in
isolation without assembling a sub-pipeline.

`RecordUnemittedPass.run` (`gir/passes/record_unemitted.py:30`) is `O(marks in model-only blocks)` —
zero in every folded program, which is all of them in production — and measures as 0.00 ms. It must
run last, because the marks it counts arrive in `ApplyMarksPass`; counting at fold time reported
zero against six real marks.

#### 20.13 The structural stage: 10.8 ms, and where it goes

`ScaffoldShapePass` (`gir/passes/scaffold_shape.py:47`) composes three sub-passes (`__init__` at
`:50`, `name` at `:55`, `run` at `:58`) and calls `am.invalidate()` between each — correctly, since
each may rewrite the CFG the next one reads. The 10.8 ms at DU512 splits as: `ShortPathFold`'s two
`_trace` walks over roughly `2 × I/2` instructions, plus `FoldShortPathPass`'s block deletion, plus
two `O(B+E)` predecessor recomputations.

* `FoldShortPathPass.run` (`gir/passes/fold_short_path.py:62`) is `O(I)` in the analysis it consumes
  and `O(B + E)` in its own work: retarget every terminator pointing at a `short` block (via the
  local `_rewire` closure, `:151`, which stamps the per-path chunk frame), delete the short blocks,
  then **recompute every block's `preds` from the rewritten terminators** using the module-local
  `_targets(term)` (`:197`). `folded(prog)` (`:49`) is an `O(1)` meta lookup.
* `EarlyExitPass.run` (`gir/passes/early_exit.py:70`) is `O(B · M)`: find the peel-validity `CondGoto`
  structurally (its false target is the drain chain head), build one `CondChain` arm per short trip
  count, record each arm's `path_chunk_base`, then recompute `preds` again with its own `_targets`
  (`:112`). `_drain_chain(prog)` (`:53`) is an `O(B)` scan keyed on `Block.phase`.
* `ScaffoldMapPass.run` (`gir/passes/scaffold_map.py:57`) is `O(B + arms)`: attach TensileLite's label
  vocabulary to each terminator, deriving the role from CFG shape (a `LoopBack` is the loop's own
  exit; a `CondGoto` whose source is a back-edge source is the loop end; otherwise it is the peel
  guard). It calls `_drain_chain` again and does an `O(M)` `drains.index(tgt)` per arm — `O(M²)`
  on `M ≤ 3`.

`Pass` (`gir/passes/base.py:15`) with `name` (`:25`) and `run` (`:28`), and `StructuralPass` (`:33`),
carry no cost; they carry the *contract* that decides where cost may be spent. The distinction is
what lets `run_pipeline` be as coarse as it is: because only a `StructuralPass` may change the CFG,
and only `ScaffoldShapePass` is one, everything after stage 1 could in principle share a single
analysis manager. It does not, because `pipeline.run_pipeline` (`gir/passes/pipeline.py:61`) calls
`am.invalidate()` after **every** pass (`:67`) rather than honouring the returned invalidation names.
The comment there calls it coarse and it is: `ApplyMarksPass` returns `("body",)` and `TokensPass`
returns `("tokens",)`, and nothing reads either. At `B = 4` throwing away `Dominators` after a body
edit costs microseconds; the reason to fix it is that it is the mechanism by which a *future*
larger CFG would degrade, and the hint plumbing is already in the `Pass.run` contract.

`_check_rotation_waw(prog, am)` (`gir/passes/pipeline.py:74`) is the post-pipeline gate: it walks
`shared_refs(prog)` once, tallying per token id how many writes and reads touch it and which
`covers` axes each side spans, then raises if a token is written and never read, or written over an
axis no read covers. `O(A + T_id)`, plus the `MemTokenAssignment` recomputation noted in §20.11. It
lives here rather than in `verify_gir` because it is a property of the *final* program, and putting
it in the verifier failed 448 of 948 tests on programs that legitimately have writes and no reads
yet.

#### 20.14 The IR itself: what the node set costs

`gir/nodes.py` imports only `dataclasses` and every node is a plain frozen or mutable dataclass, so
"cost" here means allocation count and hashing, not computation.

* **Allocation.** One `Tile` (`:33`) and one `Ref` (`:70`) per operand position per instruction. At
  `I = 1936` with roughly 2–4 refs each, the lowering allocates on the order of 6000 `Tile`s and
  6000 `Ref`s. `Tile` is `frozen=True` and hashable, so it participates in set/dict keys; `Ref` is
  not a dict key anywhere — it is keyed by `id()` (§20.18). `Tile.coord_map()` (`:49`) and
  `Tile.shape_map()` (`:52`) each build a fresh dict from the tuple, `O(|coord|)`; both are called
  from the renderer and from tests, never from an analysis inner loop.
* **`Gen` (`:57`)** — two ints, one instance per rotating buffer set, so at most four per program.
  `Move` (`:108`) and `Mma` (`:133`) are one per instruction. `Mark` (`:162`) is one per applied
  placement, 20–26 per program, validated against `MARK_KINDS` (`:157`).
* **Terminators** — one per block, so at most a dozen instances of `Bound` (`:181`), `Pred` (`:203`),
  `Goto` (`:229`), `CondGoto` (`:235`), `Trips` (`:248`), `LoopBack` (`:279`), `Return` (`:296`) and
  `CondChain` (`:309`) combined. Their render helpers `Bound.render` (`:194`), `Pred.render` (`:224`)
  and `Trips.render` (`:272`) are string formatting called only by the dump and by scaffold label
  derivation. The two validators, `Pred.__post_init__` (`:220`, checks `op` against the six legal
  comparisons) and `CondChain.__post_init__` (`:331`, rejects an empty arm tuple and any arm that is
  not a `(Pred, target)` pair), run once per construction and are `O(arms)`.
* **`successor_labels(blk)` (`:342`)** — the single authority for "what are this block's successors",
  an `O(1)` type switch returning a list. It is called from `cfg.successors`, `cfg.BackEdges.run` and
  `Program.walk_rpo`, i.e. `O(B)` times per CFG walk and `O(B)` walks per pipeline run. Free.
* **`Block` (`:370`)** with `label` (`:431`) as a property alias for `phase`; `GenPhi` (`:436`) and
  `GenXfer` (`:447`), one or two per loop header.
* **`Program` (`:459`)** — `add_block` (`:477`), `block` (`:481`) and `bump` (`:484`) are `O(1)`.
  `walk_rpo` (`:487`) with its recursive `visit` (`:495`) is `O(B + E)` with an on-stack set to skip
  back edges, then reversed, with unreachable blocks appended defensively. It is called by
  `GenReaching`, `FenceRegions`, and the renderer — three times per pipeline run at `O(B+E)` each.

`gir/region.py` costs nothing and constrains everything. `Region` (`:36`) is a frozen four-tuple
`(block, after, before, policy)` and `PendingMark` (`:59`) a mutable `(mark, region, anchor)`; 20–26
of each per program. The **opaque-anchor** decision recorded there is what makes anchor resolution a
linear scan (§20.12), and it is the right trade: it buys the ability to interleave four independent
region analyses' marks into one body without any of them holding a stale index.

`gir/analysis.py` is the cache, and it is the single most consequential 59 lines in this section.
`Analysis` (`:24`) with `cache_key` (`:33`) and `run` (`:36`); `AnalysisManager` (`:40`) with
`__init__` (`:45`), `get(analysis, prog)` (`:48`) and `invalidate(names=None)` (`:55`).

* `get` keys on `(analysis.cache_key, prog.version)`. Because the version is in the key, a mutating
  pass that bumps automatically makes every stale entry unreachable — so **`invalidate` is purely
  about dictionary size, never about correctness**, and the `names` parameter is accepted and
  ignored. That is why passing a caller's manager into `verify_gir` (§20.11) would be safe.
* `cache_key` defaults to the class name. Three analyses override it — `DepDefuseAnalysis`
  (`gir/analyses/dep_defuse.py:45`), `RegBandAnalysis` (`gir/analyses/reg_band.py:40`) and
  `GrIncrementRegions` (`gir/analyses/gr_increment.py:119`) — each to pin a stable string a class
  rename cannot change. Only `GrIncrementRegions` reproduces the default; `RegBandAnalysis` pins
  `"RegBand"` and `DepDefuseAnalysis` pins `"DepDefuse"`, both shorter than their class names. None is parameterized, so the
  cache is effectively "one entry per analysis per program version".
* The cache is **per-manager**, and there are five managers alive during one `build_gir`: the
  pipeline's, `verify_gir`'s fresh one, and one each inside `GirToRocisa.__init__`
  (`gir_to_rocisa.py:91`) and any direct analysis call. That multiplicity is where §20.11's triple
  computation comes from.

#### 20.15 The front end: `loopir_to_gir`, 36% of the budget

`lower_to_gir` (`loopir_to_gir.py:484`) is 59 ms at DU512 MIWT4 and 2.9 ms at DU64 — a factor of 20
for a factor of 20 in `I`, so it is cleanly **linear**, and the 59 ms is 30 µs per emitted
instruction of Python object construction. It is second only to `FenceRegions` and, unlike
`FenceRegions`, there is no algorithm to improve: it is allocation and dictionary work.

The walk itself, `_flatten(nodes, env, out, rel)` (`:174`), mirrors the renderer's traversal and is
where the unrolling happens: a static `Loop` is expanded over each of its `ranged_bodies()` ranges,
**copying the environment dict at every level** (`{**env, nd.mode: v}`). With a 4-level nest of
extents 4×4×4×2 that is one dict copy per node per level, so the dict-copy count is `O(I × depth)`.
Replacing the copies with a push/pop on a single mutable dict would be the single largest win in this
file and is behaviour-preserving as long as `_convert_load`/`_convert_mma` keep taking `dict(env)`
snapshots (they already do, at `:172`). Other traversal arms: a `Branch` binds its residue (pinned or
fanned over every arm), a `Peel` descends, a `Bind` binds the chunk induction (or, for the symbolic
drain value, carries the steady-relative offset in `rel`), and a `Cond` evaluates its predicate in
the current environment and descends the taken arm — an *unresolved* predicate keeping the `then`
arm as the representative path.

Per-instruction conversion:

* `_convert_load(theta, inst, env, rel, gens)` (`:348`) — the read/copy fork. Builds one `Tile` and
  one `Ref` per member, calling `_concrete_coord(op_coord, env)` (`:292`, `O(|coord|)` with an `Expr`
  evaluation per symbolic entry), `_member_region_coord(coord, op, theta)` (`:249`, which builds the
  set of *all* operands' region modes on **every call** — `O(operands × axes)` per Ref, a clean
  hoist), `_absorbed(theta, op)` (`:307`, which calls into the geometry layer's `quantum_axes` and
  then filters `theta.inner_modes()`, `O(modes)`), `_quantum_coords(coord, quantum)` (`:331`, the
  cross product over the spanned axes — 1 or 2 elements in practice), `_gen_of(gens, opname)`
  (`:327`, a dict lookup), `_expr_raw(e, env)` (`:137`, the modulus-free `Expr` evaluation that
  yields `gdelta`, `O(|terms|)`), and `_deps_of(inst)` (`:154`, `O(|awaits|)`).
* `_convert_mma(theta, inst, env, reads)` (`:429`) — one `Mma` per WMMA, projecting each source
  onto that operand's own presence so a broadcast operand does not name a location no read writes.
  `O(srcs × |coord|)`.

The control-flow translation runs once per program and is free: `_gir_bound(e)` (`:42`) converts one
`Expr` side to a `Bound` and **raises** on a mixed-radix / modulus / carry shape rather than
stringifying it; `_gir_pred(p)` (`:119`) converts a structured predicate field by field;
`_trips_of(loop_trip, per_trip)` (`:100`) reads the steady range's upper bound as a trip count;
`_op_of_token(theta, token)` (`:161`) is an `O(operands)` lookup, called per copy — another trivial
hoist; `_short_steps(els, M)` (`:55`) validates and returns the short arm's `M` per-step
`(guard, nodes)` pairs; `_drain_steps(peel_body)` (`:230`) splits the drain `Peel` at each top-level
`Bind`. `lower_to_gir._scan(nodes)` (`:520`) is the `O(nodes)` descent that finds the prologue
`Peel`, the outer `Loop`, the drain `Peel` and the peel-validity `Cond`.

The three façade functions cost only what they call: `build_gir(theta, mainloop, params, pipeline)`
(`:882`) is lower + `run_pipeline`, once per kernel and cached by the caller;
`lower_params_to_gir(params)` (`:844`) adds a θ translation and is used by tests and debug;
`gir_text(prog)` (`:850`) renders an already-built program and is wrapped in a `try` that returns a
`# …` comment on any failure — observability that can never break codegen. It is only invoked under
the `OutputLoopIR` global parameter, so it is off in a production sweep.

#### 20.16 The back end: per-stage rebuilds and per-instruction string work

`GirToRocisa` is constructed **once per emitted stage**, not once per kernel:
`KernelWriter._girEmitStage` (`KernelWriter.py:3871`) does `GirToRocisa(self, kernel, tPA, tPB,
prog).emit_block(...)`, and there are three such call sites (`KernelWriter.py:4437`, `:5330`,
`:6136`) covering the prologue, the steady body and the drain forks. Each construction
(`gir_to_rocisa.py:81`) does:

* a fresh `AnalysisManager().get(RegBandAnalysis(), prog)` — a full `O(I)` walk, per stage;
* `_register_depth(prog, band)` (`:37`) — `O(|band items|)`, or a full `O(I)` fallback walk when no
  band is supplied;
* `buildMfmaContext(kernel, tPA, tPB)` (`leaves.py:164`) — the loop-order-invariant WMMA constants,
  including capability validation and the dtype→instruction-type table lookups;
* `buildLdsReadContext(kernel, tP)` (`leaves.py:462`) twice (A and B), plus
  `buildMxScaleReadContext(kernel, mx)` (`leaves.py:364`) per scale tensor on a microscaling kernel.
  Each computes the whole LDS geometry for one operand: strides, padding, the `read_fragments`
  decomposition, the split boundary.

None of that depends on the phase, and all of it is rebuilt per phase. The contexts are dataclasses
(`MfmaTileContext`, `leaves.py:39`; `LdsReadTileContext`, `leaves.py:63`) with no back-reference to
the block, so hoisting the `GirToRocisa` instance to the same cache that already holds the `Program`
(`KernelWriter._loopModelGirCache`) is a contained change. The win is 3–5 redundant `RegBand` walks
and 9–15 redundant context builds per kernel.

`emit_block(prog, phase, tpByOperand, internalPointerSwap)` (`gir_to_rocisa.py:110`) then does one
`plan_block`, one `plan_quantum`, and a dispatch loop over the acts. Per act the fixed overhead is a
`_tag(out, phase, kind, detail)` (`:258`) — a `%`-formatted comment string plus an `addComment0`
into the module — and, for every act that produces a scaffold sub-module, an `_append_tag(code,
tag)` (`:239`) that **iterates `code.flatitems()` and rewrites every instruction's comment**. That is
`O(instructions emitted by this act)` with a string concatenation each, i.e. proportional to the
emitted stream, done twice (once by the scaffold, once here). It is the single largest constant in
the emission path and it is deliberate: an instruction-attached comment survives the downstream
scheduler's reordering where a floating comment line does not.

The remaining `GirToRocisa` members are `O(1)` or `O(small)` per act:

* `_tok(token)` (`:225`) and `_who(unit)` (`:230`) — comment formatting; `_who` joins a fused
  movement's members with `+`.
* `_emit_fence(out, phase, at)` (`:276`) — calls the scaffold's `_syncThreads` with
  `_fence_tokens(at)` (`:326`, which sorts the Mark's ids and **raises** if there are none), then
  `_register_fence(code)` (`:307`), a stack-based walk of the emitted sub-module recording every
  `SBarrier` by identity into `states.girOwnedBarriers`. `O(emitted items)`, six times per kernel.
* `_fused_tp(unit, tpByOperand, what)` (`:345`) — derives the aliasable pairs from the tensor
  parameters (`("A","B")`, plus the MX pair when both scales exist) and refuses a movement outside
  them. `O(1)`.
* `_emit_swap` (`:386`), `_emit_gr_inc` (`:415`), `_emit_region_inc` (`:508`), `_emit_copy` (`:536`)
  — each resolves the tensor parameters, calls one scaffold primitive, appends the tag.
  `_emit_region_inc` issues `|steps|` primitives in a loop (`steps` is ±1 in every shipping shape).
  `_wrap_lead(to_chunk, M)` (`:484`) is the one-line `pf − min(to_chunk, M+1)` derivation.
  `_token_ids(at)` (`:601`) converts the act's ids to a list of ints.

`leaves.py` is the per-coordinate emitter and therefore the place where cost is *supposed* to be
linear in the emitted instruction count. `LeafEmitters` (`:143`, `__init__` at `:151`) holds the
writer and the per-operand ring widths; `_ringWidth(tc)` (`:155`) is the `m = u % W` fallback lookup,
reached only when a caller supplies no slot. `emitWmmaTile(...)` (`:245`) emits exactly one WMMA
instruction, with its `_fb(tc)` closure (`:265`) as the fallback and two `_checkRegBuffer` (`:576`)
invariant guards — a single integer comparison each against `states.numVgprBuffer`.
`emitLdsReadTile(...)` (`:611`) emits **one `ds_read` per fragment** from `ctx.fragments`, a list
whose length is dtype-derived (two for bf16, four for fp8), with `_pad(off)` (`:693`) applying block
padding per fragment; the address arithmetic per fragment is a handful of integer operations plus
one `cal_offset_srcAddr` call into the scaffold's component. `emitCopyTile(...)` (`:745`) emits one
global→shared movement, routing to the single-region primitive when `regions > 1`.
`_abbrevToInstType(abbrev)` (`:126`) is a five-entry dict lookup used once per context build.

So emission is `Θ(emitted instructions)` with a comment-rewrite constant, which is the right shape.
The only super-linear risk on this path is `plan_quantum`'s `carrier_tile_of` scan (§20.9), bounded
by the merged operand's tile extent.

#### 20.17 Off the codegen path: the checkers and the geometry

Six modules cost nothing during a normal build because they either run once per kernel over a small
input, or never run at all.

**`tdm_split.py`** is pure arithmetic on scalars and is called from six other packages. `split_of`
(`:35`) is a dict lookup plus two comparisons; `split_factors` (`:57`) and `any_split` (`:69`) are
`O(1)`; `split_packs_lds` (`:76`) is a two-term boolean; `_pad` (`:104`) one division;
`TdmSplitGeometry` (`:112`) a frozen record with `isSplit` (`:141`); `derive` (`:145`) a dozen
integer operations. The one loop in the file is `wave_region_span(kernel, tc)` (`:179`), which builds
a set of region indices over `MIWaveTile[axis]` tiles — `O(MIWaveTile)`, at most 8 iterations. It is
called from `Solution.py` and the read-side components, i.e. once per operand per solution, and it is
the reason `Solution.py` can decide the split gate without importing anything that pulls in `rocisa`.

**`lds_geometry.py`** is the same story: `region_split_is_packed` (`:94`), `region_row_elems`
(`:110`), `fold_inner_offset` (`:135`), `addr_coord_on_split_axis` (`:163`), `tile_row` (`:191`),
`tiles_per_region` (`:231`) and `region_bytes` (`:245`) are each a handful of integer operations, all
`O(1)`, all called once per emitted read from `leaves.emitLdsReadTile`. `read_fragments(blockWidth,
bpeDS, lrvw, inputPerThUnroll, matrixInstK)` (`:33`) is the one with a loop: a nested comprehension
over `nOuter × nInner` producing the fragment list — at most four elements — and it is called once
per operand per context build, not per read. `LANE_INTERLEAVE` (`:30`) is the scaffold's constant,
kept here rather than re-derived so the two cannot drift.

**`region_derivation_check.py`** is test-only. `TileCtx` (`:45`) and `Finding` (`:59`) are records;
`rows_per_region(ctx)` (`:67`) is one division; `check_tiles(ctx)` (`:72`) loops over
`MIWaveTileAxis` tiles (≤ 8) comparing the index-derived and position-derived region for each, plus
one divisibility floor check; `describe(ctx)` (`:97`) formats a summary line. `O(MIWaveTile)`.

**`uniform_emission.py`** is the one off-IR checker that runs in production, once per kernel, from
`KernelWriter.py:11500`. Its input is the whole emitted stream, so `n` here is **instructions in the
`.s` file** — tens of thousands, three orders of magnitude larger than `I`. Cost:

```
    items   := list(rootModule.flatitems())                       # O(N) with N = emitted stream
    regions := agent_discriminating_regions(items)                # O(N) + O(branches × LOOKBACK)
    at      := {id(b): position for our barriers}                 # O(N)
    findings: for each owned barrier, for each region, is it inside?   # O(|owned| × |regions|)
```

`agent_discriminating_regions(items)` (`:148`) makes two `O(N)` passes: one indexing label positions,
one testing each item with `_branch_target(item)` (`:110`, a class-name prefix test) and, on a hit,
`_condition_kind(items, i)` (`:129`). That last is the expensive primitive: it walks back up to
`_LOOKBACK = 12` items calling `_text(item)` (`:97`), which does **`str(item)`** on a rocisa
instruction and strips the comment. So the real cost is `12 × branches` full instruction
renderings — hundreds to low thousands per kernel. `_is_label(item)` (`:106`) is a class-name test.
The final cross product is `O(|owned barriers| × |regions|)`, measured across the fleet at ~0.8 owned
barriers against ~1.7 regions per kernel, so it is nothing. `UniformEmissionError` (`:174`) derives
from `RuntimeError` specifically so a finding costs one kernel rather than the whole build;
`check_uniform_placement(rootModule, ownedBarriers, kernelName)` (`:214`) is the entry point.
If this check ever shows up in a profile, the fix is to cache `_text` per item index rather than
re-rendering the same instruction up to twelve times for twelve different branches.

**`asm_lane_eval.py` and `lds_region_check.py`** are an offline diagnostic pair with **no in-tree
caller**: `lds_region_check.check` is invoked by hand against an emitted `.s` file. Their cost never
touches a build, but it is the one place in the package with a genuinely large multiplier, so it is
worth stating.

`LaneEval` (`asm_lane_eval.py:49`, `__init__` at `:56`) is a per-lane interpreter: every VGPR is a
**list of 32 values**, and every VALU instruction is executed by a list comprehension over the lanes.
So `step(op, dst, srcs)` (`:261`) costs `O(nlanes)` per instruction, with `read(operand, lane)`
(`:111`) and `write(operand, value_list)` (`:145`) as the `O(1)` accessors called `2–3 × nlanes`
times each. The float helpers `_f32` (`:194`), `_b32` (`:196`), `_f64` (`:198`), `_b64` (`:200`) are
`struct` conversions; `_stepf(op, dst, srcs)` (`:202`, with its `rd64` closure at `:221`) and
`_step64(op, dst, srcs)` (`:239`) handle the float and 64-bit integer opcodes and return `True` when
they consumed the instruction. `lanes_of(vgpr_index)` (`:379`) copies the lane list.
`UnsupportedInstruction` (`:41`) is raised for any opcode not in the tables — never skipped, because
a skipped instruction leaves a stale register and yields an address that looks plausible and is
wrong. Total cost: `O(slice length × nlanes × nwaves)`, where the slice is the *backward slice* of
the address registers, typically a few hundred instructions. Seconds, not milliseconds, but only
when a human asks.

`lds_region_check.py` is the driver. `parse_symbols(lines)` (`:86`) evaluates the `.set` table in
file order — `O(lines)` with an `eval` per entry; `parse_instructions(lines, sym)` (`:183`) is
`O(lines × tokens)` regex work calling `_operand(tok, sym)` (`:100`), `_defines_first_operand(op)`
(`:155`) and `_operand_width(tok, sym)` (`:163`) per line; `collect_ds_loads(lines, sym)` (`:237`) is
another `O(lines)` regex pass. `backward_slice(insts, targets)` (`:207`) is one reverse pass with a
live set, `O(instructions × width)`. `check(path, region_bytes, …)` (`:253`) ties them together and
then runs `LaneEval` once per wave over the slice. `DsAccess` (`:55`) with `regions(region_bytes,
lds_base)` (`:63`) buckets the per-lane addresses into regions, `O(nlanes)`; `Violation` (`:73`) is
a record. The whole thing is `O(file size)` plus the interpreter, and it exists because re-deriving
the address in Python would be a *transcription* of the emitter — a checker that agrees with the
kernel exactly when both are right and exactly when both are wrong the same way.

**`gir/render.py`** is `O(I)` string formatting, invoked only under `OutputLoopIR`. `render_gir(prog)`
(`:304`) walks every block and every instruction, calling `_move_line(mv)` (`:124`) or `_mma_line(mm)`
(`:131`) per instruction, each of which calls `_ref_str(ref)` (`:67`) per `Ref`, which in turn calls
`_coord_str(coord)` (`:21`), `_gen_str(ref)` (`:25`) and `_covers_str(ref)` (`:55`);
`_dep_str(inst)` (`:82`) and `_token_str(mv)` (`:101`) add the dependency and token annotations.
`_term_line(term)` (`:152`) and `_pred_str(p)` (`:137`) render the terminator; `_short_loop_lines`
(`:170`) and `_theta_facts_lines` (`:234`) render the two header blocks from `prog.meta`.
`gir_counts(prog)` (`:348`) is a second `O(I)` pass tallying reads, copies and WMMAs per block with
the `model_only` flag alongside. Roughly 20 string operations per instruction, so a few milliseconds
at the largest shape — paid only when someone asked for the dump.

#### 20.18 The data structures that are the bottleneck, and what replaces them

Five representation choices account for essentially all the avoidable cost.

**(a) `frozenset` of integers as an interval.** `fence_regions._admissible_slots` materialises up to
`n_slots` Python ints per hazard; measured 242,310 elements at the largest shape, and the greedy
`argmax` then does ~248,000 membership tests against them. Every admissible set is either an interval
`(a, b]`, a prefix `[0, p]`, or the **complement** of an interval — three shapes, all `O(1)` to
represent. The replacement is a *difference array*: for each hazard, `+1` at the start of each of its
(at most two) runs and `−1` past the end; one prefix sum over `n_slots` then gives the coverage count
of every slot in `O(H + n_slots)` per round instead of `O(H × n_slots)`. The greedy choice and its
tie-break to the earliest slot are unchanged, so the emitted fences are bit-identical. This is the
single largest win available and it is confined to one function plus its caller.

**(b) Repeated linear scans over the whole program, once per unit.** `swap_regions._units`,
`_ring_of` and `_requirements`, and `gr_increment._units` and `_reqs`, each walk every instruction in
the program. With two hops × two units × three scans, `SwapRegions` alone touches every instruction
twelve times. The replacement is one bucketing pass: `{(hop, unit): [(block, inst, ref)]}` built once
in `run`, from which the unit list, the rings and the per-block requirements all fall out. Same
answers, `O(I)` instead of `O(U_hop · I)`.

**(c) `id()`-keyed maps.** Three results key on object identity: `Reaching._by_ref`
(`gir/analyses/gen_reaching.py:28`), `MemTokenSet._per_ref` (`gir/analyses/mem_tokens.py:87`), and
`DepDefuse._raw`/`_war` (`gir/analyses/dep_defuse.py:26-27`). This is *fast* — a dict on small ints —
and it is correct because each result object retains `prog`, so the identities stay live. It is also
the package's sharpest edge: a pass that replaces a `Ref` rather than mutating it silently orphans
every entry, and there is no check that would notice. All three are correctly hidden behind a query
API (`Reaching.of`, `MemTokenSet.tokens_for`, `DepDefuse.raw`/`war`) so no caller ever writes `id(...)`
itself — that encapsulation is the mitigation, and it should be preserved by any replacement. If the
invariant ever needs to be enforced rather than documented, give `Ref` a monotonic integer `uid`
assigned at construction and key on that; the maps stay `O(1)` and a rebuilt `Ref` becomes a visible
miss rather than an invisible one.

**(d) Tuple coordinates as dictionary keys.** `Tile.coord` is a tuple of `(mode, value)` pairs and is
hashed constantly — as part of `short_path`'s consumer keys, `quantum`'s group keys, and
`verify_dataflow`'s register names. Hashing a 6-element tuple of `(str, int)` pairs is roughly 12
hash operations, and the coordinate is re-hashed at every use because nothing caches it. Two cheap
improvements, in increasing order of intrusiveness: intern the mode-name strings once at lowering
time so the string hashes are cached (CPython already caches `str.__hash__`, so this is mostly
automatic and the point is to avoid *building* new strings per instruction); or give `Tile` a
`__hash__` cached in a slot. Neither is worth doing today — the measured cost is inside the 30 µs per
instruction that `loopir_to_gir` spends anyway.

**(e) `prog.meta` dictionary probes in the innermost loop.** `emit_plan._plan_move` and `_plan_mma`
re-read five to seven `meta` keys and rebuild two to four `set`s **per instruction**, and
`tokens._unit_key` does a linear scan of `meta['unit_regions']` per instruction. Every one of those
is a pure function of `prog.meta`, which does not change during planning. Hoisting them into a small
context object built once per `plan_block` call is a mechanical change worth roughly a third of the
6 ms plan cost and a good fraction of `TokensPass`'s 5.3 ms.

**Dead weight and duplicated derivations, in full.** These cost nothing measurable and are listed
here because an optimiser reading the code will trip over each of them and wonder whether it is
load-bearing. None is.

* `refs._tile_axis_of(coord)` (`gir/refs.py:142`) and `refs._extent_hint(ref)` (`:150`) — vestiges of
  the abandoned preimage form of `covered_coords`. `grep -rn` finds only their definitions. Delete,
  together with `covered_coords`'s accepted-and-unused `extent` parameter (`:105`).
* `fence_regions._already_fenced` (`gir/analyses/fence_regions.py:107`) accepts `doms` and
  `reachable` and reads neither: the separator test (`_separates`, `:161`) subsumes dominance and
  reachability in one predicate, and the parameters were left behind when it replaced them. Dropping
  them also lets `FenceRegions.run` stop asking for `Dominators` (`:263`) — a small, real saving of
  one analysis, and more importantly it removes a false signal that the cover depends on the
  dominator tree.
* `swap_regions._topo` (`gir/analyses/swap_regions.py:178`) and `gr_increment._topo`
  (`gir/analyses/gr_increment.py:255`) are the same Kahn topological sort written twice, differing
  only in a comment. Both callers compute `order` and — since the rewrite onto
  `ValuePlacementSolver` — `SwapRegions.run` **never uses its result**: it builds `order` at `:244`
  and passes only `all_preds`/`all_succs` to `_flow`. `GrIncrementRegions` does still use it, for
  `_units`' first-seen ordering and for the `reqs` dict. So one copy is dead code and the other
  should move to a shared helper.
* `swap_regions._unemitted_edges(prog, headers)` (`:150`) accepts `headers` and ignores it, so the
  two call sites can share one signature. Harmless; documented at the definition.
* `verify_dataflow._RegFile.snapshot()` (`gir/verify_dataflow.py:74`) has no caller in the package.
* `Pass.run`'s invalidation-name return value: `ApplyMarksPass` returns `("body",)`, `TokensPass`
  returns `("tokens",)`, `FoldShortPathPass` returns `("ShortPathFold",)`, and
  `AnalysisManager.invalidate(names)` ignores the argument. The plumbing exists end to end and does
  nothing; either honour it (§20.19 item 2's companion) or delete it, but leaving it half-wired is
  how a future maintainer concludes that fine-grained invalidation is already implemented.

#### 20.19 Ranked optimisation opportunities

Ordered by measured win divided by risk. "Win" is milliseconds off the 165 ms worst-case build;
"risk" is the chance of changing emitted output. Every item is actionable as written — none needs
further analysis first.

**1. Represent admissible fence slots as intervals, not integer sets.** *Win: ~45 ms (27% of the
build) at the worst shape, ~1 ms at the common one. Risk: low.*
Rewrite `fence_regions._admissible_slots` (`gir/analyses/fence_regions.py:51`) to return one or two
`(lo, hi)` half-open runs, and rewrite `_cover` (`:75`) to score slots with a difference array:
accumulate `+1`/`−1` at each run's endpoints across the still-uncovered hazards, prefix-sum once, and
take the argmax with the existing earliest-slot tie-break. Complexity goes from
`O(rounds · n_slots · H)` with a set-membership constant to `O(rounds · (H + n_slots))` with an
integer-array constant. The chosen slots are provably the same because the score function and the
tie-break are unchanged. **Pin it with a test that asserts the fence Marks are identical before and
after on the `loop_copies=2` fixture and on a 4-wave DU512 shape** — the two configurations where
the cover has more than one round.

**2. Let `verify_gir` accept the caller's `AnalysisManager`.** *Win: ~14 ms. Risk: very low.*
`verify_gir(prog, expect_steady_loops="one")` (`gir/verify.py:422`) creates a fresh manager at `:432`
and thereby recomputes `LdsHazards` and `MemTokenAssignment` from scratch. Add an optional `am=None`
parameter defaulting to a fresh one, and have `run_pipeline` (`gir/passes/pipeline.py:69`) pass its
own. **Safety is structural, not a judgement call**: `AnalysisManager.get` keys on
`(cache_key, prog.version)`, so an entry computed against a different version is unreachable. Do the
same for `_check_rotation_waw` (`:74`), which already takes `am` but receives one that
`run_pipeline` invalidated on the line above — moving the `invalidate()` call to *before* each pass
instead of after fixes that half for free.

**3. Bucket the program once per pointer analysis instead of rescanning per unit.** *Win: ~3 ms.
Risk: low.*
In `SwapRegions.run` (`gir/analyses/swap_regions.py:227`) and `GrIncrementRegions.run`
(`gir/analyses/gr_increment.py:122`), replace the `_units` / `_ring_of` / `_requirements` (and
`_units` / `_reqs`) rescans with a single pass building `{(hop, unit): [(block_label, inst, ref)]}`.
The three derived quantities — the unit list in first-seen order, the ring, and the per-block
requirement list — are all projections of that map. Keep `_hop_access` (`:77`) and `_copy_of`
(`gir/analyses/gr_increment.py:66`) as the predicates; only the iteration changes.

**4. Pass a precomputed plan into `check_plan` from codegen.** *Win: ~12 ms. Risk: none.*
`KernelWriter.py:3803` calls `check_plan(prog)`. Change it to
`check_plan(prog, plans=plan_program(prog))`. The parameter already exists and is already threaded
through all three checks (`gir/verify_dataflow.py:277`). Better still, keep that plan on the same
cache entry as the `Program` so `GirToRocisa.emit_block` reuses it instead of re-planning per stage —
that turns four more `plan_block` calls into dictionary lookups, worth another ~6 ms.

**5. Hoist the per-instruction `meta` reads in `emit_plan` and `tokens`.** *Win: ~4 ms. Risk: low.*
Build a small frozen context in `plan_block` (`gir/emit_plan.py:296`) holding `reduction_modes`,
`free_modes` as pre-built sets per operand, `inner_order`, `mode_extents`, `operand_regions`,
`region_modes` as pre-built sets, `mma_inputs`, and the derived `scale_of` map — then pass it to
`_plan_move` and `_plan_mma` instead of having each rebuild them. Do the same for
`tokens._unit_key` (`gir/passes/tokens.py:52`), which currently linear-scans `meta['unit_regions']`
twice per instruction: precompute `{operand: unit_key}` once in `TokensPass.run`.

**6. Cache `GirToRocisa` per kernel rather than per stage.** *Win: 3–5 `RegBand` walks and 9–15
context builds per kernel; likely 2–5 ms. Risk: medium.*
`KernelWriter._girEmitStage` (`KernelWriter.py:3871`) constructs a new emitter per stage. The
contexts it builds are loop-order- and phase-invariant by construction, so one instance per kernel is
sound. **Medium risk** because the emitter captures `writer`, `tPA` and `tPB`, and the three forks do
not necessarily pass the same tensor-parameter objects — verify that first, and key the cache on
`(kernelName, id(tPA), id(tPB))` if they differ.

**7. Push/pop the environment in `_flatten` instead of copying it.** *Win: 5–10 ms of the 59 ms
lowering. Risk: medium.*
`loopir_to_gir._flatten` (`:174`) builds `{**env, mode: v}` at every level of every nest. Replace
with a single mutable dict plus explicit set/restore around each recursive call. **Medium risk**
because the leaf conversions must keep taking `dict(env)` snapshots (they already do, at `:172`) —
if any consumer ever retains the live dict, this silently aliases every instruction's environment.
Add an assertion in the leaf that the snapshot is a distinct object before making the change.

**8. Hoist `needing_fence()` and `on_path` out of their per-item loops.** *Win: <1 ms. Risk: none.*
`FenceRegions.run` calls `hazards.needing_fence()` (an `O(H)` scan building an `H`-element tuple)
once per block inside the RPO loop (`gir/analyses/fence_regions.py:275`); compute it once before the
loop. `UniformPlacement.run` rebuilds `on_path` per fence (`gir/analyses/uniform_placement.py:145`)
although it depends only on the enclosing block; memoise it per label.

**9. Replace `seq.count` with a `Counter` in `check_source_coverage`.** *Win: <1 ms. Risk: none.*
`gir/verify_dataflow.py:214` is `O(n²)` in the reads per operand. One line.

**10. Index block bodies before resolving anchors.** *Win: negligible today. Risk: none.*
`PlacementPass._slot` (`gir/passes/placement.py:47`) and `ApplyMarksPass._anchor_index`
(`gir/passes/apply_marks.py:45`) are identity linear scans, giving `O(P · L)`. Build `{id(node): i}`
per block once. **Do this only if the Mark count ever becomes proportional to the body length** —
today `P = 20` regardless of shape, and the scan is honest, obvious code.

**11. Delete the unused `DepDefuseAnalysis` request in `TokensPass`.** *Win: ~0.2 ms. Risk: none.*
`gir/passes/tokens.py:124` computes it "for consistency" and discards it.

**12. Fuse the verifier's four full-program walks.** *Win: ~2 ms. Risk: none.*
`_check_gen_ssa`, `_check_noiter`, `_check_semantic` and `_check_operands` each walk `_all_insts`
independently. One pass collecting all four pieces of evidence, then four assertion loops over the
collected evidence, is mechanical. Do it only if the verifier ever matters; the current form is far
easier to read and each check raises with its own precise message.

Three things deliberately **not** on the list:

* **The CFG walks.** `Program.walk_rpo`, `cfg.successors`, `_reachable`, `_separates`, `_topo`,
  `_loop_blocks`, `_reachable_from`. All `O(B + E)` or `O(B²)` on `B ≤ 12`. Optimising them is
  negative value: they are the clearest code in the package and they are free.
* **The `ValuePlacementSolver` fixpoints.** `antic` and `avail` converge in one or two rounds over
  four blocks; `ValuePlacementSolver.__init__` (`gir/analyses/value_placement.py:104`) just stores
  the seven inputs. Making the sweep worklist-driven would add a worklist to save nothing.
* **The token machinery.** `T_id = 4`. Any structure indexed by tokens is already optimal.

#### 20.20 Where the invalidation would have to go

Every caching proposal above runs into the same question: the passes mutate the graph, so what
happens to a cached fact when they do? The answer differs by *what* is cached, and getting it wrong
is a miscompile rather than a slowdown. Three tiers:

**Tier 1 — cached across the whole pipeline, invalidated by `prog.version`.** Anything an `Analysis`
returns. `AnalysisManager.get` (`gir/analysis.py:48`) already handles this and it is airtight,
because the version is part of the key rather than a flag consulted separately. The only obligation
on a pass author is `prog.bump()`, and `Pass`/`StructuralPass` (`gir/passes/base.py:15`, `:33`) state
it as the contract. **Any new cache should be an `Analysis`** — that is the cheapest correct place to
put one, and it is why items 2 and 3 of §20.19 are safe.

**Tier 2 — cached within one pass or one call, never stored on the Program.** The `meta` context of
item 5, the bucketing of item 3, the difference array of item 1. These live for the duration of one
`run()` and the program cannot change under them, because a pass either mutates or reads, never both
in the same phase. `CollectPendingMarksPass`, `PlacementPass`, `RegGenPass` and
`RecordUnemittedPass` mutate nothing at all; `TokensPass` mutates only `Move.token`/`token_ids`,
which no analysis it calls reads; `ApplyMarksPass` mutates bodies and is the last body mutator.
**No invalidation is needed at this tier and none should be written** — a cache with a lifetime
shorter than the thing it caches is the one shape that cannot go stale.

**Tier 3 — cached on the writer, across the *emission* of several blocks.** This is item 4's plan
cache and item 6's `GirToRocisa` cache, and it is the only genuinely delicate tier, because the
program is finalized by then but the *writer* is not: `KernelWriter` calls `_girEmitStage` three
times with different `internalPointerSwap` flags and potentially different tensor-parameter objects.
The invariants that make it safe are (a) `plan_block` is a pure function of `(prog, phase)` and the
program is not mutated after `build_gir` returns — nothing in `gir_to_rocisa` or `leaves` writes to a
GIR node — and (b) the leaf contexts are functions of `(kernel, tP)` only. Both are true today and
neither is *checked*. If item 6 is implemented, the honest thing is to key the cache on
`(prog.version, kernelName)` and assert the version has not moved, so that a future pass that runs
between stages fails loudly instead of emitting from a stale plan.

The one invalidation bug that would be easy to introduce: caching anything keyed on a **node
identity** across `ApplyMarksPass`. Insertion does not invalidate node identities — `list.insert`
moves references, it does not copy nodes — so `id(node)` maps survive. But *indices* do not, which is
exactly why `Region` holds opaque anchors rather than positions, and why an index map for item 10
must be built after the last insertion into that block, not before.

#### 20.21 What the tests pin, and what they do not

The unit suite is 602 collected tests in `Tests/unit/test_gir.py` plus 29 in `Tests/unit/test_gir_to_rocisa.py` (191 and 23 `def test_` functions, parametrized — see §19.3.1),
over the fixtures in `Tests/unit/gir_fixtures.py` (the canonical bf16 NT KMN kernel at
MI 16×16×32, DepthU 64, PGR2, and its PLR0 / single-LDS / fused / multi-agent variants). For this
section the relevant observation is a negative one: **there is no performance test anywhere in the
package, and no test asserts a complexity bound.** Every fixture is a DepthU 64 kernel with a
19-instruction steady body, which is the smallest shape in §20.2 — the shape where the entire
pipeline costs 8 ms and the `FenceRegions` cover is 2 ms.

That is not an argument for adding timing assertions (they are flaky and they measure the machine).
It is an argument that **the fixtures do not exercise the regime where any of this matters**, and a
maintainer implementing §20.19 item 1 must construct the large shape by hand to see the difference at
all. The `loop_copies=2` fixture is the exception worth knowing about: it is the only configuration
in the suite where the fence cover has cross-block work to do and where `_already_fenced` /
`_separates` are non-vacuous, so it is the right correctness gate for any change to `_cover`.

What the tests *do* pin, and what makes the optimisations above safe to attempt, is the **output**:
the suite asserts the exact Marks placed, the exact token ids, the exact fence slots and the exact
emit-plan act sequence for each fixture. Combined with the two byte-identity harnesses the project
runs against generated assembly, that is the real safety net — an optimisation that changes an
answer will fail a named assertion rather than a timer.

#### 20.22 How to reproduce these numbers

No build is required and no GPU is involved: the whole measured path is pure Python plus the
`Tensile.LoopModel` package. From `tensilelite/`:

```python
import time
from Tensile.LoopModel import translate
from Tensile.LoopModel.decoder import emit_mainloop
from Tensile.Lowering import lower_to_gir
from Tensile.Lowering.gir.passes.pipeline import pipeline
from Tensile.Lowering.gir.analysis import AnalysisManager

theta = translate.params_to_theta(PARAMS)          # any TensileLite param dict
prog  = lower_to_gir(theta, mainloop=emit_mainloop(theta))
am    = AnalysisManager()
for p in pipeline():                               # per-pass wall time
    t = time.perf_counter(); p.run(prog, am); am.invalidate()
    print("%-28s %7.2f ms" % (p.name[:28], 1000 * (time.perf_counter() - t)))
```

To attribute a pass to its analyses, ask each one on a **fresh** `AnalysisManager` so the timing
includes its dependencies; to attribute an analysis internally, `cProfile` it and sort by `tottime` —
the greedy-cover generator expression at `gir/analyses/fence_regions.py:100` is the marker to look
for. The shape knobs that move `n` are `DepthU`, `MIWaveTile`, and `NumWaves` (the last changes
nothing structural but turns every hazard cross-agent, which is what makes `FenceRegions` do work).
`PrefetchGlobalRead` moves `M` and therefore the block count.

Two figures in this section came from instrumenting rather than timing, and are worth recomputing
the same way after any change to the fence cover:

```python
total = sum(len(_admissible_slots(h, len(prog.blocks[h.consumer.block].body) + 1,
                                  h.consumer.block))
            for h in hazards.needing_fence())      # 784 at DU64/4w, 242310 at DU512 MIWT4/4w
```

and the fence count itself — **6 fences for 1284 cross-agent edges** at the largest shape. That
ratio is the justification for the whole set-cover design over one-Mark-per-obligation, and it is
the number to watch: if a change makes the fence count grow toward the edge count, the cover has
stopped batching and the emitted kernel will over-synchronize long before the compile time becomes a
problem.
